content.content:
# 02 Engine

The engine is everything below the screens: the typed mod project, the pipeline that turns it into artifacts, the test and delivery machinery, and the per-feature generators. All of it is **built** on the integration branch `feature/cyrus-r2` (see [11 history](11-history.md)), behind switches that default OFF ([reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md)). Each section ends with *Verified* (what actually ran) and *Not verified* (honest gaps); the per-feature long form with numbers is in [`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`](../DOCUMENTATION.md) (heading list: [reference/documentation-index.md](reference/documentation-index.md)).

Contents: [ModSpec and revisions](#modspec-revisions-namespaces) / [router and adapters](#capability-router-and-adapters) / [version registry](#version-registry) / [build pipeline and service](#build-pipeline-and-the-build-service) / [Test Flight](#test-flight) / [delivery](#delivery-orchestrator-and-rollback) / [managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting](#managed-plugins-pack-loader-pack-hosting) / [conflict engine and Mod Packs](#conflict-engine-and-mod-packs) / [import](#import-your-own-mod) / [data packs and worldgen](#data-packs-and-worldgen) / [creatures](#creatures) / [designers](#gameplay-designers) / [item states](#item-model-states-and-display-contexts) / [config studio core](#config-and-stats-core) / [motion core](#motion-core) / [meshgen and Blender](#ai-mesh-meshgen-and-blender) / [playtest, Doctor, telemetry](#playtest-bots-server-doctor-health-telemetry) / [Try It](#try-it-server) / [multi-version and legacy 1.21.1](#multi-version-builds-and-the-1211-legacy-path) / [networking and AI capabilities](#mod-capabilities-networking-and-ai) / [Mod lifecycle](#mod-lifecycle) / [eval](#eval-harness)

## ModSpec, revisions, namespaces
- **What.** `ModSpec` v1 (`lib/cyrus/engine-core/spec.ts`, Zod + committed JSON Schema `modspec.v1.schema.json`) is the game-agnostic content IR: items, mobs, abilities, GUIs, quests, recipes, loot, assets, datapacks, config, dependencies, acceptance tests. A project is an immutable chain of **revisions** (`revisions.ts`, `store.ts`); every revision traces to exact inputs and the engine release that built it; the last passing revision is always kept; revert = a new revision. Tables `CyrusProject`, `CyrusRevision` (a DB trigger keeps revisions immutable; smoke checks `cyrus_revision_immutable`), `CyrusProjectAsset`, `CyrusIdentifier`.
- **Namespaces and identifiers.** Each project reserves `nx_<hash>` at creation so ids, keys, permissions, sound keys, glyph codepoints and model paths are collision-free by construction (`identifiers.ts`; glyph block allocation for HUD fonts).
- **Plan gate.** `asset-gate.ts`: free/katara no assets, saka sound, all sound + texture; only create/edit is gated; fails closed.
- **Release record.** `release.ts`: engine release id (prompt version + sheets + rules + scanner hash + image digest), source/classpath/output hashes, scan report per build.
- **Compatibility.** Before r0 a "project" was a chain of `ModBuild` rows (`rootBuildId`/`baseBuildId`); both exist, the engine tables are additive (manual SQL `2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core.sql`, **not applied** in production).
- Verified: unit + DB tests (`cyrus-engine-core`, `cyrus-engine-store-db`). Not verified: production data migration.

## Capability router and adapters
- **Router** (`engine-core/router.ts`, deterministic, no model): classifies what a request needs (plugin / plugin + resource pack / datapack / future client mod), discloses limits ("a vanilla client cannot show X"), applies the tier gate, and **downgrades instead of erroring**. The studio's separate broad-request router (`lib/cyrus/route.ts`, pure, zero API calls) routes prompts to games/categories/open mods.
- **Adapters** (`lib/cyrus/adapters`): the `GameAdapter` contract = artifact types and routes, toolchain + scanner, version list, knowledge source, **asset delivery per asset kind**, install rules, test lane, maturity (planned / template / beta / stable), route rules, optional `AssetProfile` (formats, channels, delivery, worker class, legal). Adapter #1 is Minecraft; `motion-minecraft.ts` lowers motion. Generated matrix: [reference/adapters.md](reference/adapters.md).
- **Per-game support packs** (`lib/cyrus/games/*.ts`, `GameSupport`): verified knowledge for Terraria, Valheim, Zomboid (and Palworld/Rust on WIP branches). These are knowledge + validators + compile harnesses only; those games are template previews in the UI and **on hold**.

## Version registry
`lib/cyrus/versions/registry.json` + `registry.ts`: the single source for JDK, pack formats (resource + data, major.minor), Paper API coordinate, **exact Paper server build and sha256 pin** (what Test Flight boots), capability flags (`legacyCustomModelData`, `dialogApi` ...), status (supported / preview / legacy / blocked) and `buildable`. Fail closed: a `null` pack number or missing server pin blocks the feature. Contract-tested against Paper's Fill API; a nightly check creates a "preview" row for new versions. Rendered table: [reference/versions.md](reference/versions.md). Facts: 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11 build on JDK 21; 26.1.2 (build 74) and 26.2 (build 133) need JDK 25 and are **registered but not buildable** until the image has JDK 25 and an eval ran; 26.3 has only alpha/beta Paper builds, so it stays unpinned preview (an early research claim that 26.3 was stable was wrong and is corrected). `resourcePackClientVerified=false` everywhere: no real Minecraft client has loaded a Cyrus pack.

## Build pipeline and the build service
- **Service** `services/modbuilder` (Docker image on VM 88001; see [07 operations](07-operations.md)): `server.js` (HTTP), `prompts.js`, `route.js` (complexity routing, tiers), `precheck.js` + `rules/failure-rules.json` (18 reviewed rules), `sheets/` (per-version API sheets), `autofix.js` (deterministic fixes before a model repair), `scan.js` (bytecode + source safety scan), `jar.js` (reproducible jars: `jar --date`, sorted inputs), `release.js`, plus asset/designer/datapack/creature/config modules that bundle the `lib/cyrus` validators. Builds run Claude CLI with Read/Write/Edit only in a throwaway workspace, `javac --release N -proc:none` against a pre-resolved Paper-only classpath (Gradle only builds classpath files), no network for the model.
- **Models by tier**: Katara = Haiku class, Saka = Sonnet, Yakko = Opus (`MB_TIER_*`); complexity routing picks cheaper models for simple requests; repairs escalate one tier after two failed repairs. Knobs (all off by default): `MB_EFFORT`, `MB_CACHE_TTL`, `MB_DEDUPE`.
- **Portal side** `lib/modbuilder/create.ts` (`createModBuild`: validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap, token gate), `lib/cyrus/builder` (HTTP client), `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` (NDJSON re-attachable stream: stage -> `think`, `/live` draft -> `file`/`chunk`).
- **History**: service 0.3 (tuning) -> 0.4 (images the AI reads + live code) -> 0.5 (usage metering, auto-fixes, lean tools, cost knobs; branch only) -> 0.6 (networking capability manifest) -> r0+ (engine release record, asset/design/datapack/creature/config sections, catalog tools, designer no-model builds, legacy textures, JDK 25). Only 0.4 is running on VM 88001 per the last deploy; the rest requires the rebuild in the runbook.
- Verified: eval 28/28 built, 13/13 loaded on v6 (pre-programme); the programme added 178 eval prompts (harness built, **no paid run yet**). Not verified: AI output quality for texture/sound/datapack/import/designer/meshgen specs (no paid model build has run for them).

## Test Flight
`lib/cyrus/testflight` + `scripts` runner on node-2: a disposable Paper server per target version (pinned jar + sha256), boot, plugin enabled, RCON commands, `datapack list`, log matcher, clean shutdown; honest **per-check status table** (no "success" if a required stage was skipped); label "boot-tested" only where it ran. Measured: 26.x boots in about 10.4-10.8 s (722-803 MB RSS), 1.21.11 on JDK 21 in 18 s (878 MB); a whole flight 12-35 s. The **gate** (`CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE`, worker sweep) flies each succeeded build; `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL` refuses installs of failed builds. One flight at a time (node-2 build lock); no container limits yet. Real flight records live in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/*flights*.json` ([09 testing](09-testing-and-verification.md)).

## Delivery orchestrator and rollback
`lib/cyrus/delivery` + `lib/cyrus/assets` + worker: journaled install / update / uninstall of a jar, resource pack, data pack, worldgen pack or Mod Pack as one unit, through the existing Mods engine (`GameMod` source `cyrus` + `ServerMod` + worker `GAME_MOD_SYNC`; state file on the guest, backup, staged write, rollback). Honest states `rolled_back` and `rollback_incomplete`; Mod Packs re-check conflicts against the live server inside the orchestrator. Enqueue API `POST /api/cyrus/delivery/v1` (same checks as install, restart/worldgen acknowledgements, idempotency key, one job per server): contract in [CYRUS-DELIVERY-API.md](../CYRUS-DELIVERY-API.md). Flags `CYRUS_DELIVERY`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`, `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL`, `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL`. Verified on real node-2 Paper: install, update, a deliberately broken update rolled back, uninstall, worldgen rollback, and (r38) a revoke mid-update that first failed to roll back (bug found and fixed) then restored exact bytes. Not verified: any customer server (by rule).

## Managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting
- **Managed plugins** (`lib/cyrus/managed`, tables `CyrusManagedPlugin`, `CyrusServerManagedPlugin`): plugins Nxeon installs because Cyrus mods depend on them, pinned per Minecraft family, ref-counted, not removable while depended on. Hosts the **Nxeon Pack Loader** and **BetterModel 3.5.0** (MIT). Seed script `scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts`.
- **Pack Loader**: sends N packs by UUID with `addResourcePack`, per-pack required/optional, accept-rate telemetry, Geyser/Floodgate detection; `server.properties` only as a fallback (it holds just one pack). The conflict engine detects an existing pack owner (ResourcePackManager, Oraxen, Nexo).
- **Pack hosting** (`lib/cyrus/packhost`): content-addressed immutable URLs `/p/<sha1>.zip`, size caps (`CYRUS_PACK_MAX_BYTES`), retention GC, local or S3-compatible store (`CYRUS_PACK_STORE`); production with nothing configured has NO store (fail closed). The provider is not named to customers. Provider/domain choice is an open owner action.

## Conflict engine and Mod Packs
- **Inventory** (`lib/cyrus/inventory`): read-only scan of jars' descriptors (bytecode summary, plugin.yml, Fabric/Quilt/Forge/NeoForge descriptors), `server.properties`, datapacks, existing pack owners.
- **Static conflict engine** (`lib/cyrus/conflicts`, pure and deterministic: same input gives a byte-identical report): plugin names, commands/aliases (incl. Brigadier roots), permissions, depend/softdepend DAG, api-version/Java/Folia, events and priorities, NamespacedKey/PDC keys, legacy `custom_model_data` ints and `item_model` keys, recipe keys, sound keys, single-owner resources (Vault providers, chat, tab, sidebar), datapack `replace:true`, pack whole-file overrides, font codepoint overlap, budget classes. Severity: blocking / warn / info. Reserved namespaces prevent most clashes. A mutation corpus (take a good mod, collide IDs) tests catches.
- **Mod Packs** (`lib/cyrus/modpack`, API `/api/cyrus/modpacks/v1`, `CYRUS_MODPACKS`): an Nxeon manifest shaped like mrpack (files with path/sha1/sha512/downloads/env, override dirs, platform=paper); third-party jars by URL + hash, only Cyrus-built artifacts embedded; versioned; compatibility matrix; installs and rolls back as one unit; never contains Paper/vanilla jars. **Every open warning must be acknowledged** to install (owner recommendation applied, r29). Not plan-gated. r32 fix: pack create/install now enforce the same networking-consent and Test Flight gates as single installs. UI screens exist (r31).

## Import your own mod
`lib/cyrus/import` + `services/modbuilder/import.js`: source-only. Copies `src/main/{java,resources}`, ignores the uploader's build files (their build is never run), compiles with the service template and a **curated checksum-pinned dependency allowlist** (`import/deps.json`; first-class integrations Vault, LuckPerms, PlaceholderAPI). Unsupported: Kotlin, Lombok, annotation processors. Ingestion limits (zip-slip, zip-bomb ratio, nested jars, multi-release, class major), no execution at ingestion, ownership attestation record, detected licence, public sharing hard-off. Two scan profiles: strict for generated, **attested/imported** with warnings and no "safe" claim. Imported source becomes revision 0 and uses the same change planner, tests, versions and install path. Jar-only imports are analysis only. Not plan-gated (model use and assets follow tokens and gates). Flag `cyrus_import_enabled`. Fixed: import refused 1.21.9+ data packs (r31).

## Data packs and worldgen
`lib/cyrus/datapack`, `services/modbuilder/{datapack-spec,datapacks}.js`, `scripts/cyrus/datapack-derive.py`: a typed spec compiled by per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation (including a command allowlist and `line_continuation` refusal) then a real headless Paper over RCON. Content: recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. **Worldgen** (R4: custom dimensions, biomes, structures; `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`): `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so these need a restart and a **broken worldgen pack stops a server at its next start**; hence delivery rollback is mandatory. Spans four datapack schemas and two `pack.mcmeta` styles (`min_format/max_format` from 1.21.9). Verified: worldgen showcase passed on 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11/26.1.2/26.2; broken files each alone (validator 8/8, server refuses to start 7/8). Flags `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`, `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`.

## Creatures
`lib/cyrus/creature` + `services/modbuilder/creatures.js` (`CYRUS_CREATURES`): `RigSpec` (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips, 32 bones/creature, 4 creatures per server caps) compiled to a Blockbench `.bbmodel` for **BetterModel 3.5.0** (managed plugin, needs Java 25, so animated creatures are 26.x first; 1.21.x gets a vanilla-model mob with custom skin + full sound set, e.g. the banshee). Base vanilla mob supplies hitbox/AI; display entities carry the bones. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL). Verified on real Paper 26.2: load, pack hand-off + Pack Loader, malformed models, perf ramp 1/10/50; r30: creature paint is byte-identical inside BetterModel's pack. Not verified: how it looks or animates in a real client.

## Gameplay designers
All behind `CYRUS_DESIGNER` (+ `CYRUS_DESIGNER_BUILDS` for no-model builds). Design files live in `assets/designs/<id>.json` with a top-level `kind`; the compiler (`lib/cyrus/designer`, 39 files) emits a complete Paper plugin from a **verified Java component library**; every number/text becomes a `config.yml` setting, so edits change config only (proved with a config migration on real servers). Static + runtime **Budget** caps, no `run_command`, no arbitrary scripts. Javadoc/escape injection fixed in r32 (AC-3).
- **Item + ability graph (R3)**: 10 triggers, 11 conditions, 21 actions, 17-component library.
- **Menu + quest (R3)**: chest menus (click/drag cancel hardening, pagination, item/XP/Vault money prices, permissions, dialogues), quests (chains, 7 objective kinds, branches, daily/weekly, per-player progress in PDC).
- **Boss + encounter (R4)**: 20 vanilla bases, 1-5 one-way phases, up to 8 telegraphed attacks, arena (leash, enrage), boss bar, capped minions, drops by damage share, wave encounters; never persistent, no griefing.
- **HUD + glyphs (R4)**: action bar, per-player boss bars, per-player sidebar (never replaces another plugin's), plus the mod's own font `<ns>:hud` with codepoints from the identifier registry; 15 glyph presets; no shaders, no free positioning (the router says so).
- Verified by Test Flight RCON on 1.21.11 (JDK 21) and 26.2 (JDK 25): item, menu/quest, boss (55 RCON + 2 log checks), HUD (22 checks); scripted Mineflayer player 5/5 for the boss. Not verified: a real client seeing menus/HUD/bosses; other versions have no javac classpath for designers.
- **Designer edits reach servers (r31)**: no-model designer builds (config.yml-only = the base jar repacked with only config.yml changed; structural = javac) + delivery; real flight: edit -> build -> deliver -> RCON shows cooldown 100 and config migrated v1 -> v2. Image rebuild needed before enabling.

## Item model states and display contexts
`lib/cyrus/itemmodel` (`CYRUS_ITEM_STATES`): `ItemModelSpec` v1 with per-category defaults for **8 display contexts** (gui, ground, item frame, first/third person hands, head) and named STATES (bow pull stages, gun aim/reload) selected by 1.21.4+ item model definitions (`condition`, `range_dispatch`, `select`, plugin-set custom_model_data flags). No free animation (frame animation via `.mcmeta`, fast model switching). Vanilla-verified emitter and a real node-2 runner (javac 1.21.11 + 26.2, strict scan, Test Flight self-check, component round trip). The handgun grip default sits about 2/16 block off the hand in third person; the proposed fix is `CYRUS_HANDGUN_GRIP_FIX` (off, changes shipped packs, owner's call).

## Config and stats core
`lib/cyrus/config` (`CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO`): `ConfigSpec` v1 (12 param types, hard limits vs a "balanced" band, units, `applies` live/reload/restart, `visual` viewport links, presets), 12 category templates as data (mob, melee, gun, armor, ability, boss, shop, quest ...), the AI declares tunables and the build verifies they are read, **values-only revisions** delivered through the orchestrator (no model, no build), schema inference for imported mods. Real flights on 1.21.11 + 26.2; the "send to server" API returned 501 until the worker path landed (r31 closed it for designers). UI: [03 studios](03-studios.md).

## Motion core
`lib/cyrus/motion` (game-neutral, pure; plan: [motion/MOTION-PLAN.md](motion/MOTION-PLAN.md)): `MotionSpec` v1 with typed tracks (transform, particle, sound-cue, light/material, event/state-machine), deterministic `sample`, analytic seeded particles, a state-machine runner, simulation + event log, structured validation against a game capability's caps. 9 presets (gun fire, gun fire/reload/cock machine, hinged door, parametric humanoid/quadruped/floating gait generators, muzzle flash, explosion, fire, smoke, water splash). **Minecraft lowering** = designer kind `motion`: display-entity interpolation segments, step snaps, particle births, sound keys. Vehicles are explicitly NOT a Minecraft target (the core can express them; the build waits for a vehicle game). Real flights 39/39 RCON on 1.21.11 + 26.2; headless software-rasteriser sheets for review. Not verified: any look in a real client; studio timeline/preview build-out is future work.

## AI mesh (meshgen) and Blender
`lib/cyrus/meshgen` + `blender/` (`CYRUS_MESHGEN`, `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH`; layer 4 of Model Studio): Zod specs for templates (rifle, crate, sword), a parts kit (10 shapes), a deterministic router over a **cost ladder** (rung 0 template ... rung 3 scratch script behind an AST guard), run headless in Blender 5.2.2 LTS inside a transient systemd sandbox (no network, user nobody, read-only fs, memory/CPU/task caps, build lock). Real node-2 flights accepted rifle/crate templates (1.4-2.5k triangles in about 26-29 s). Estimate-first job route + durable file queue + 30 s worker tick; the r32 driver-expression scan bypass (AC-2) is fixed. Not verified: a real model call, LODs, in-engine load, kernel escape (a microVM/gVisor is required before scratch scripts), an isolated GPU/worker; "drum magazine looks like a wheel"; parts overlap rather than union. Layer-3 meshes have **no export target** (no supported game takes glTF).

## Playtest bots, Server Doctor, health telemetry
- **Playtest** (`lib/cyrus/playtest`, `CYRUS_PLAYTEST`): a ModSpec's functional acceptance tests compile deterministically into a plan of 14 step kinds run by a Mineflayer bot inside Test Flight; verdict kept apart from the boot verdict. Ran on 1.21.11: a good fixture passed 6/6 and a deliberately broken one failed exactly the right checks. Other versions are refused, not skipped. Generated builds store no ModSpec yet, so playtest reports "not run" for them.
- **Server Doctor** (`lib/cyrus/doctor`, `CYRUS_SERVER_DOCTOR`, admin-only read-only API): server facts, plugin/mod inventory, conflicts, problems, warnings. Tested on a throwaway server seeded with a conflict, a throwing plugin, a legacy plugin and a Fabric mod; never run on a customer server.
- **Telemetry** (`lib/cyrus/telemetry`, `CYRUS_HEALTH_TELEMETRY`): opt-in, aggregate-only signals, retention; signed ingest answers 503 until the DRAFT tables exist; no collector exists. Open security items O-1 (replay) before enabling.

## Try It server
`lib/cyrus/tryit` (`CYRUS_TRY_IT`, `CYRUS_TRY_IT_EXPOSE`): a throwaway Paper server on node-2 with caps and auto teardown so a visitor can try a mod. Real flight: create -> pack served -> RCON -> a second session refused -> teardown. **Not public**: needs the firewall range 47200-47299 and DNS.

## Multi-version builds and the 1.21.1 legacy path
- `lib/cyrus/matrix` (`CYRUS_BUILD_MATRIX`): one design builds for several versions; real per-version compile + flight on 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11 all passed; 26.2 refused as preview. Not wired into the builds route or stored yet.
- Legacy 1.21.1 item looks (`CYRUS_LEGACY_TEXTURES` portal, `MB_LEGACY_TEXTURES` service): custom model data on 52 vanilla-verified carriers, pack format 34, damage states only, every other limit shown; real Paper 1.21.1 flight 6/6. No real client.

## Mod capabilities: networking and AI
`lib/cyrus/capabilities.ts` + `services/modbuilder/capabilities.js` (default OFF, setting `cyrus_mod_networking_enabled`): a mod that wants the network ships an `nx-capabilities.yml` manifest (declared host allow-list, anti-SSRF via the NxHttp wrapper), the customer consents at install, and AI calls go through the Nxeon AI gateway (`lib/cyrus/ai-gateway*.ts`, a budgeted stub that never calls a model yet; gateway token expiry is open item O-2).

## Mod lifecycle
`lib/cyrus/lifecycle` + worker sweeps: install plans, on/off, broken/outdated detection (`cyrus-compat-watch`), updates, creator warnings. Game-version rules come from `GameSupport`.

## Eval harness
`lib/cyrus/eval`, `scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts`, `services/modbuilder/eval/`: 178 prompts in categories with a per-version matrix and scoring spec; one-command runner with dry run, budget cap (required for a real run), resume, stage scoring, `baseline.json` + `report.md`. First run planned: 90 builds on 1.21.11 at Saka tier, estimated $9.73-$22.23. **No paid run has happened**; tested only against a fake CLI. See [09 testing](09-testing-and-verification.md).

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)

#!/bin/bash
# Build one Test Flight fixture plugin jar the way the build service does (javac --release N -proc:none against the
# version's resolved classpath file, reproducible `jar --date`). Runs on the build host; fixtures are trusted code.
#   build.sh <fixture-dir> <api-version> <java-home> <release 21|25> <classpath.txt> <out.jar>
set -euo pipefail
SRC="${1:?fixture dir}"; API="${2:?api-version}"; JH="${3:?java home}"; REL="${4:?release}"; CP="${5:?classpath file}"; OUT="${6:?out jar}"
W="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$W/classes"
"$JH/bin/javac" -J-Xmx768m --release "$REL" -proc:none -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$(tr -d '\n' < "$CP")" -d "$W/classes" $(find "$SRC/src" -name '*.java' | sort)
sed "s/@API@/$API/" "$SRC/plugin.yml" > "$W/classes/plugin.yml"
( cd "$W/classes" && find . -type f | sed 's#^\./##' | sort > "$W/entries" )
args=(); while read -r e; do args+=(-C "$W/classes" "$e"); done < "$W/entries"
"$JH/bin/jar" --create --file "$OUT" --date 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z "${args[@]}"
sha256sum "$OUT"

# Paper API 1.21.11 cheat sheet
Verified against paper-api-1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT (the exact jar you compile against). Names here are correct for 1.21.11; do not use names from other versions.

## Attributes (org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute)
- In 1.21.11 `Attribute` is an INTERFACE (registry-backed, not an enum). Constants have NO prefix. GENERIC_* / PLAYER_* names DO NOT EXIST here.
- Use: MAX_HEALTH, MOVEMENT_SPEED, ATTACK_DAMAGE, ATTACK_SPEED, ATTACK_KNOCKBACK, ARMOR, ARMOR_TOUGHNESS, KNOCKBACK_RESISTANCE, SCALE, JUMP_STRENGTH, GRAVITY, STEP_HEIGHT, SAFE_FALL_DISTANCE, FALL_DAMAGE_MULTIPLIER, FOLLOW_RANGE, FLYING_SPEED, LUCK, BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED, BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE, ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE, SNEAKING_SPEED, SPAWN_REINFORCEMENTS, TEMPT_RANGE, CAMERA_DISTANCE.
- Keys: minecraft:scale, minecraft:max_health (no 'generic.'). `Attribute.valueOf/values()` are deprecated for removal and you cannot `switch` on an Attribute: look up by key with `Registry.ATTRIBUTE.get(NamespacedKey.minecraft("scale"))` (may return null).
- `entity.getAttribute(attr)` returns AttributeInstance or null: always null-check. Methods: getBaseValue(), setBaseValue(double), getValue(), getDefaultValue(), addModifier(m), addTransientModifier(m), removeModifier(Key), getModifier(Key), getModifiers().
- Modifiers: `new AttributeModifier(new NamespacedKey(plugin, "growth"), amount, AttributeModifier.Operation.ADD_NUMBER)` (optional 4th arg EquipmentSlotGroup). Operations: ADD_NUMBER, ADD_SCALAR, MULTIPLY_SCALAR_1. The UUID/String constructors are deprecated for removal. Remove the old modifier with `removeModifier(key)` before adding it again with the same key.
- Size changes: the default scale is 1.0; setBaseValue on the scale attribute or use one keyed modifier. Max health: set the attribute first, then `setHealth(Math.min(h, attr.getValue()))`.

## Sounds (org.bukkit.Sound)
- In 1.21.11 `Sound` is an INTERFACE, not an enum: no `switch`, `Sound.valueOf/values()` are deprecated for removal. Look up config names with `Registry.SOUNDS.get(NamespacedKey.minecraft("entity.player.levelup"))` (may be null).
- e.g. ENTITY_PLAYER_LEVELUP, BLOCK_NOTE_BLOCK_PLING, BLOCK_NOTE_BLOCK_HAT, UI_BUTTON_CLICK, UI_TOAST_CHALLENGE_COMPLETE, ENTITY_EXPERIENCE_ORB_PICKUP, ENTITY_ENDER_DRAGON_GROWL, ENTITY_WITHER_SPAWN, ENTITY_ENDERMAN_TELEPORT, ENTITY_VILLAGER_NO.
- `player.playSound(player.getLocation(), Sound.X, 1f, 1f)`. Version-proof for config strings: `player.playSound(net.kyori.adventure.sound.Sound.sound(Key.key(name), net.kyori.adventure.sound.Sound.Source.MASTER, 1f, 1f))`.

## Particles (org.bukkit.Particle, an enum in every version)
- Old names DO NOT EXIST. Old -> new: REDSTONE->DUST, SPELL_WITCH->WITCH, VILLAGER_HAPPY->HAPPY_VILLAGER, VILLAGER_ANGRY->ANGRY_VILLAGER, SMOKE_NORMAL->SMOKE, SMOKE_LARGE->LARGE_SMOKE, EXPLOSION_NORMAL->POOF, FIREWORKS_SPARK->FIREWORK, ENCHANTMENT_TABLE->ENCHANT, TOTEM->TOTEM_OF_UNDYING, ITEM_CRACK->ITEM, BLOCK_CRACK->BLOCK, SPELL_MOB->ENTITY_EFFECT, CRIT_MAGIC->ENCHANTED_HIT, DRIP_WATER->DRIPPING_WATER. Unchanged: FLAME, HEART, NOTE, CRIT, END_ROD, CLOUD, PORTAL, SOUL_FIRE_FLAME.
- Particles that REQUIRE data (spawning them without it fails at runtime): DUST needs `new Particle.DustOptions(Color.RED, 1.0f)`; DUST_COLOR_TRANSITION needs Particle.DustTransition; ENTITY_EFFECT needs a `Color`; ITEM needs an ItemStack; BLOCK, FALLING_DUST, BLOCK_MARKER, DUST_PILLAR need BlockData (`Material.STONE.createBlockData()`); SCULK_CHARGE needs Float; SHRIEK needs Integer; VIBRATION needs Vibration; TRAIL needs `new Particle.Trail(targetLocation, Color, durationTicks)`; BLOCK_CRUMBLE needs BlockData; TINTED_LEAVES needs a Color; EFFECT and INSTANT_EFFECT need `new Particle.Spell(Color, float power)`; DRAGON_BREATH needs a Float; FLASH needs a Color.
- `world.spawnParticle(Particle.FLAME, loc, count, offX, offY, offZ, extraSpeed)`; with data: `world.spawnParticle(Particle.DUST, loc, 10, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0, new Particle.DustOptions(Color.AQUA, 1f))`. For a config value use `Particle.valueOf(name.toUpperCase())` inside try/catch.

## Potion effects and enchantments (same names in all 1.21.x)
- PotionEffectType old -> new (old names DO NOT EXIST): INCREASE_DAMAGE->STRENGTH, SLOW->SLOWNESS, FAST_DIGGING->HASTE, SLOW_DIGGING->MINING_FATIGUE, JUMP->JUMP_BOOST, DAMAGE_RESISTANCE->RESISTANCE, HEAL->INSTANT_HEALTH, HARM->INSTANT_DAMAGE, CONFUSION->NAUSEA. Unchanged: SPEED, REGENERATION, FIRE_RESISTANCE, INVISIBILITY, NIGHT_VISION, GLOWING, LEVITATION, SLOW_FALLING. New in 1.21.11: BREATH_OF_THE_NAUTILUS.
- `new PotionEffect(PotionEffectType.SPEED, 30 * 20, 1)` = Speed II for 30 s (amplifier 0 = level I). Extra ctor args: (type, ticks, amp, ambient, particles, icon). `PotionEffect.INFINITE_DURATION` exists. `entity.addPotionEffect(effect)`. getByName is deprecated: for config strings use `Registry.EFFECT.get(NamespacedKey.minecraft("speed"))` (or Registry.MOB_EFFECT).
- Enchantment old -> new (old names DO NOT EXIST): DAMAGE_ALL->SHARPNESS, DAMAGE_UNDEAD->SMITE, DAMAGE_ARTHROPODS->BANE_OF_ARTHROPODS, DURABILITY->UNBREAKING, DIG_SPEED->EFFICIENCY, LOOT_BONUS_BLOCKS->FORTUNE, LOOT_BONUS_MOBS->LOOTING, ARROW_DAMAGE->POWER, ARROW_KNOCKBACK->PUNCH, ARROW_FIRE->FLAME, ARROW_INFINITE->INFINITY, PROTECTION_ENVIRONMENTAL->PROTECTION, PROTECTION_FALL->FEATHER_FALLING, OXYGEN->RESPIRATION, WATER_WORKER->AQUA_AFFINITY. Unchanged: MENDING, SILK_TOUCH, FIRE_ASPECT, KNOCKBACK, THORNS. New in 1.21.11: LUNGE.
- `meta.addEnchant(Enchantment.SHARPNESS, 5, true)` (true = ignore level limits) or `item.addUnsafeEnchantment(ench, level)`. Enchantment.getByName and Registry.ENCHANTMENT are deprecated; for config strings use `RegistryAccess.registryAccess().getRegistry(RegistryKey.ENCHANTMENT).get(NamespacedKey.minecraft("sharpness"))` (io.papermc.paper.registry).

## Materials and entity types
- Material.SHORT_GRASS (plain GRASS does not exist), GRASS_BLOCK, CLOCK, PLAYER_HEAD, SPAWNER, TURTLE_SCUTE, ARMADILLO_SCUTE. CHAIN was renamed: use Material.IRON_CHAIN in 1.21.11.
- EntityType: ITEM (not DROPPED_ITEM), FIREWORK_ROCKET, TNT, LIGHTNING_BOLT, SNOW_GOLEM, MOOSHROOM, END_CRYSTAL, EXPERIENCE_ORB, FISHING_BOBBER, ARMOR_STAND, CREAKING. Boats are per wood: OAK_BOAT, SPRUCE_BOAT, ..., OAK_CHEST_BOAT, BAMBOO_RAFT (BOAT/CHEST_BOAT do not exist). Thrown potions: SPLASH_POTION, LINGERING_POTION (POTION no longer exists).
- Spawning: `world.spawn(loc, Zombie.class, z -> { z.customName(Component.text("Giant", NamedTextColor.RED)); z.setCustomNameVisible(true); })` configures the mob before it appears. Get the killer with `entity.getKiller()` (Player or null).
- `world.setGameRule(GameRule.KEEP_INVENTORY, true)`; GameRule has KEEP_INVENTORY, DO_DAYLIGHT_CYCLE, DO_WEATHER_CYCLE, DO_MOB_SPAWNING, MOB_GRIEFING, FALL_DAMAGE, PVP (new in 1.21.11; SPAWN_CHUNK_RADIUS was removed). The String getGameRuleValue/setGameRuleValue are deprecated for removal. Time/weather: world.setTime(1000)/setTime(13000), setStorm(false), setThundering(false).

## Text: Adventure Components (never ChatColor or String setters)
- `Component.text("Hi", NamedTextColor.GREEN)`, `.append(...)`, `.decorate(TextDecoration.BOLD)`; MiniMessage: `MiniMessage.miniMessage().deserialize("<gold>Hi <player>", Placeholder.unparsed("player", name))`. Config text with & codes: `LegacyComponentSerializer.legacyAmpersand().deserialize(s)`. Plain string from a Component: `PlainTextComponentSerializer.plainText().serialize(c)`.
- Send: player.sendMessage(Component), Bukkit.broadcast(Component), player.sendActionBar(Component), player.showTitle(Title.title(main, sub, Title.Times.times(Duration.ofMillis(500), Duration.ofSeconds(3), Duration.ofMillis(500)))). Tab name: player.playerListName(Component). Team prefix: team.prefix(Component).
- Deprecated String APIs (avoid): ChatColor, Bukkit.broadcastMessage, sendTitle(String..), setDisplayName/setPlayerListName/setLore(String), setJoinMessage/setQuitMessage/setDeathMessage, createInventory(holder, size, String), Team.setPrefix(String). Use the Component versions: joinMessage(c), quitMessage(c), deathMessage(c), meta.displayName(c), meta.lore(list).
- Chat: listen to `io.papermc.paper.event.player.AsyncChatEvent` (AsyncPlayerChatEvent is deprecated). `event.message()` / `event.message(Component)`, `event.setCancelled(true)`, `event.renderer((source, displayName, message, viewer) -> ...)`. It runs off the main thread: read only thread-safe data (use a ConcurrentHashMap) and hop back with `Bukkit.getScheduler().runTask(plugin, ...)` before touching players/worlds.

## Commands (the build validates plugin.yml)
- Declare every command in plugin.yml (`commands: name: {description, usage, permission}`) and register with `getCommand("name").setExecutor(handler)` (+ `.setTabCompleter`). Implement `onCommand(CommandSender sender, Command command, String label, String[] args)`; check `if (!(sender instanceof Player player))` for player-only commands; validate args.length and parse numbers inside try/catch. Subcommands: switch on args[0].
- Do not use Brigadier, LifecycleEvents.COMMANDS or JavaPlugin.registerCommand(BasicCommand): the build service only accepts plugin.yml commands.

## Scheduler, threads, data, config
- `Bukkit.getScheduler().runTaskTimer(plugin, () -> {...}, delayTicks, periodTicks)` (20 ticks = 1 s), runTaskLater, runTask; or `new BukkitRunnable(){ public void run(){... cancel(); } }.runTaskTimer(plugin, 0L, 20L)`. Keep the BukkitTask to cancel it. Start a BukkitRunnable with its own runTaskTimer(plugin, ...); passing a BukkitRunnable to the scheduler's runTask*/runTaskTimer throws UnsupportedOperationException at runtime. runTaskAsynchronously only for file IO, never Bukkit API calls. Servers are Paper/Purpur, so do not use the Folia region schedulers. In onDisable save synchronously: once disabling, the scheduler rejects new tasks (IllegalPluginAccessException) and an async save is lost.
- PersistentDataContainer: `NamespacedKey key = new NamespacedKey(plugin, "soulbound")`; `ItemMeta m = item.getItemMeta(); m.getPersistentDataContainer().set(key, PersistentDataType.BOOLEAN, true); item.setItemMeta(m);` then `pdc.has(key, PersistentDataType.BOOLEAN)` / `pdc.get(key, type)` / `getOrDefault`. Types: BYTE, SHORT, INTEGER, LONG, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, STRING, BYTE_ARRAY, INTEGER_ARRAY, LONG_ARRAY, TAG_CONTAINER, LIST (`PersistentDataType.LIST.strings()`). Players and entities have getPersistentDataContainer() too. `item.editPersistentDataContainer(pdc -> ...)` exists in this version.
- Config: put defaults in src/main/resources/config.yml, call saveDefaultConfig() in onEnable, read with getConfig().getInt("path", def) / getString / getStringList / getConfigurationSection(path) (may be null), reloadConfig() on /x reload. The class is `org.bukkit.configuration.file.FileConfiguration` (NOT org.bukkit.configuration.FileConfiguration).
- Data files: `File f = new File(getDataFolder(), "data.yml"); YamlConfiguration y = YamlConfiguration.loadConfiguration(f); ... y.save(f)` (save throws IOException: catch it). Store per-player data under the UUID string. Locations and ItemStacks can be stored directly: y.set("home", loc), y.getLocation("home"), y.getItemStack("item").

## Events you will commonly need
- Register: `getServer().getPluginManager().registerEvents(listener, this)`; methods annotated `@EventHandler` (optionally `(ignoreCancelled = true, priority = EventPriority.HIGH)`).
- PlayerJoinEvent (player.hasPlayedBefore()), PlayerQuitEvent, PlayerDeathEvent (getPlayer(), getDrops(), getItemsToKeep(), setKeepInventory(bool), deathMessage(Component)), PlayerRespawnEvent (setRespawnLocation), EntityDeathEvent (getEntity().getKiller(), getDrops()), EntityDamageEvent (getCause() == EntityDamageEvent.DamageCause.FALL), EntityDamageByEntityEvent (getDamager() may be a Projectile: check `instanceof Projectile p && p.getShooter() instanceof Player`), BlockBreakEvent, BlockPlaceEvent, PlayerInteractEvent (check `event.getHand() == EquipmentSlot.HAND`, getClickedBlock() may be null), PlayerMoveEvent (fires constantly: use `event.hasChangedBlock()` first), EntityExplodeEvent/BlockExplodeEvent (`blockList().removeIf(...)`).
- TNTPrimeEvent (org.bukkit.event.block): getCause(), getPrimingEntity(), getPrimingBlock(). There is NO getIgnitingEntity().

## Menus (chest GUIs)
- Make a holder class: `class Menu implements InventoryHolder { final Inventory inv = Bukkit.createInventory(this, 27, Component.text("Warps")); public Inventory getInventory(){ return inv; } }` (size a multiple of 9, max 54). Open with player.openInventory(menu.getInventory()).
- In InventoryClickEvent: `if (!(event.getInventory().getHolder(false) instanceof Menu menu)) return; event.setCancelled(true);` then use getRawSlot() (< inventory size = top menu), getCurrentItem() (may be null), isLeftClick()/isRightClick()/isShiftClick(), `event.getWhoClicked()` (cast to Player). Also cancel InventoryDragEvent for menus. Never identify menus by title.

## Items and recipes
- `ItemStack.of(Material.DIAMOND, 5)` or `new ItemStack(mat, n)`. `item.editMeta(meta -> { meta.displayName(Component.text("Super", NamedTextColor.GOLD).decoration(TextDecoration.ITALIC, false)); meta.lore(List.of(Component.text("..."))); meta.setUnbreakable(true); meta.addItemFlags(ItemFlag.HIDE_ENCHANTS); meta.setEnchantmentGlintOverride(true); })`. getItemMeta() is null for AIR. Hand: player.getInventory().getItemInMainHand() (getItemInHand is deprecated); setHelmet(item).
- 1.21.11 also has ItemMeta.customName(Component), setItemModel(NamespacedKey), setEquippable, setUseCooldown, setGlider and io.papermc.paper.datacomponent.DataComponentTypes (experimental: prefer ItemMeta). setCustomModelData(Integer) is deprecated here (use CustomModelDataComponent) but compiles.
- give items: `player.getInventory().addItem(item)` returns leftovers (HashMap) to drop with world.dropItemNaturally. `player.give(items)` also exists.
- Recipes: `ShapedRecipe r = new ShapedRecipe(new NamespacedKey(plugin, "super_pickaxe"), result); r.shape("DDD", " S ", " S "); r.setIngredient('D', Material.DIAMOND_BLOCK); r.setIngredient('S', Material.STICK); Bukkit.addRecipe(r);` unlock with player.discoverRecipe(key); Bukkit.removeRecipe(key) in onDisable. ShapedRecipe(ItemStack) without a key is deprecated.

## Boss bars and scoreboards
- Adventure boss bar: `BossBar bar = BossBar.bossBar(Component.text("Boss"), 1.0f, BossBar.Color.RED, BossBar.Overlay.PROGRESS); player.showBossBar(bar); bar.progress(f); player.hideBossBar(bar);` progress must stay within 0..1 (clamp it). Colors PINK BLUE RED GREEN YELLOW PURPLE WHITE; overlays PROGRESS, NOTCHED_6/10/12/20. Hide it from everyone when done and in onDisable.
- Sidebar: `Scoreboard sb = Bukkit.getScoreboardManager().getNewScoreboard(); Objective o = sb.registerNewObjective("side", Criteria.DUMMY, Component.text("Title")); o.setDisplaySlot(DisplaySlot.SIDEBAR); o.numberFormat(NumberFormat.blank()); o.getScore("line").setScore(3); player.setScoreboard(sb);` (NumberFormat is io.papermc.paper.scoreboard.numbers.NumberFormat). The registerNewObjective overloads that take a criteria String are deprecated. Score entries must be unique strings (max 15 lines); keep one scoreboard per player and update scores instead of recreating it every tick; reset changed lines with sb.resetScores(entry).

## Main class traps
- JavaPlugin defines final isEnabled(), setEnabled(boolean), getServer(), getDataFolder(), getDescription(), plus getConfig(), saveConfig(), reloadConfig(), getLogger(), getName(), getCommand(). Do not declare methods with those names in your main class (use names like isFeatureOn()).

content.thinking:
I'm noting gaps in the datapack lane: advancement triggers are somewhat limited and could cover more cases like location or block interactions, and enchantment effects only cover value-based ones rather than entity effects like applying mob effects, ignite, or summoning lightning on attack.

Adding entity effect components like "post_attack" would significantly expand custom enchantment possibilities, letting datapacks create enchantments that actually do things to entities, not just modify stats — this is a high-value area since those components only exist from 1.21 onward. Loot tables, villager trades, and recipes seem mostly covered already, though I'm considering whether recipe results could carry food or consumable components since item components in recipe results have been supported since 1.20.5.

Given the massive token budget but limited time, I need to prioritize concretely: step three should implement enchantment entity effects (post_attack with apply_mob_effect, ignite, lightning, particles, sound) and attribute modifiers while equipped, with careful attention to version differences like how attribute IDs changed format between 1.21.1 and 1.21.4+. This will require updating the mcdoc validation files and figuring out how to actually test this live, possibly via RCON commands to grant enchantments.

For verification, since /enchant needs a player target, I'm thinking a loot table approach using set_enchantments would work better -- spawning the loot via RCON and confirming it drops successfully proves the enchantment resolves correctly in the registry without needing a real player.

Beyond that, I should also consider food/consumable component version branching for recipe results, and expand advancement triggers (location/biome entry, block placement, taming, breeding, dimension changes) since these are cheap wins that support the quests/advancements archetype well.

I also notice the HUD designer is missing a tab list header/footer component alongside its existing action bar and bossbar support, plus title announcements -- that's worth adding. Block look-alike placement via item displays and villager trade tables feel heavier and less essential given the effort involved, so I'll prioritize the tab list, advancement triggers, and possibly the food component work, each requiring validator, compiler, and simulator support plus real flight testing -- but first I need to finish steps one and two.

content.thinking:
Custom food is already partly handled through item design's consumable system, so I don't need a separate mechanism there. I have enough grounding now to draft the matrix—I'll write it as a machine-readable JSON file first, then build the golden corpus afterward, setting up the build harness on node-2 in parallel since iteration takes time.

Rather than hand-writing the markdown doc separately, I should generate it from the JSON via a committed script so the two never drift out of sync—something like scripts/cyrus/mc-coverage.ts that both validates the JSON shape and renders the markdown, with a `--check` mode for CI. I'll pair this with a test file that verifies the JSON parses correctly, lanes are valid, every archetype has required fields, the rendered doc matches what's committed, referenced golden corpus directories exist, and eval prompts exist for each archetype. For lane naming, I'm planning to reuse the fix-agent lane conventions plus a plugin-specific addition.

Now I'm sketching out the archetype list, aiming for roughly 60 entries, each needing an id, label, category, lanes, plugin flag, coverage details, version notes, vanilla client feasibility, limits, failure modes, golden corpus reference, and eval keys. I'm starting with commands/utility and chat-related archetypes — things like essentials-style utility commands, chat formatting, spam/swear filtering, staff/local/global channels, private messaging and offline mail, auto-broadcast announcers, and join/leave messages with MOTD and first-join kits.

I'm continuing through homes, warps with GUI, spawn/tpa with cooldowns, back/random-teleport, a custom economy (noting Vault integration isn't possible per the rules), admin shop GUIs tied to pricing, chest/sign shops, player auction houses (flagging dupe risk and persistence complexity), kits with cooldowns as a golden case, and custom permission/rank systems built on native permission attachments since LuckPerms isn't available — I'm noting the scanner will flag that as a risk.

Now I'm weighing rankup progression, chunk-based land claims with trust systems, region protection flags like pvp-off zones, and a lightweight anti-grief block logger similar to CoreProtect, while acknowledging its rollback and storage limits. I'm also considering moderation features like mute/warn/freeze/vanish, and double-checking whether ban-related API calls conflict with the rule against granting operator-level permissions.

I continue mapping out vanish for staff mode, AFK detection, playtime tracking with daily rewards and login streaks, and noting that vote rewards would need Votifier-style networking which isn't feasible, so a substitute daily reward command makes sense instead. Discord webhook integration is similarly blocked by default networking restrictions, so I'm marking that as limited or unavailable, while scoreboard sidebars, tab list headers/footers with prefixes, boss bars, titles, action bar announcements, and floating-text holograms using TextDisplay are all achievable through the plugin or HUD design since they're vanilla-feasible from 1.19 onward.

For NPCs, I'm thinking through using a mob with AI disabled that responds to clicks with commands or dialog, since player-skinned NPCs would need packet manipulation that's off-limits, though I want to check if the new Mannequin entity type (possibly added around 1.21.9-1.21.11) could work as a vanilla alternative. I'm also planning custom weapons with special abilities, armor sets with set bonuses and distinct worn appearances (checking whether worn-armor textures are supported in the texture lane), custom enchantments combining datapacks with plugin-driven effects, and custom potion brewing recipes.

Moving through more content types: custom consumable foods, custom crafting/smelting recipes via datapack or plugin, villager/wandering trader trade customization through the Merchant API, loot table and mob drop customization, advancement trees paired with designed quests, boss design, custom mobs built on vanilla bases with tweaked stats and AI, and spawner/mob-behavior customization using Paper's Pathfinder and Goal APIs.

I continue cataloging pets that follow players via the Goal API, rideable mounts and vehicles (noting the PlayerInputEvent steering limitation only applies from 1.21.3+, so 1.21.1 is restricted to vanilla rideables), and arena-style minigames like spleef or TNT run requiring lobby/countdown/team logic and careful world-reset handling.

Moving through more plugin ideas: duel arenas with kits, parkour courses with checkpoints and leaderboards, mcMMO-style job/skill leveling, cosmetic effects like hats and particle trails, timed world events with weather/time voting, and custom worldgen with biomes and structures. I also note that custom block "furniture" is only achievable through item displays plus barriers since true new block types aren't possible, before moving into HUD glyph concepts.

I'm thinking through custom music discs and ambient region music, noting that 1.21+ introduced a jukebox_song datapack registry and jukebox_playable item component, which could enable fully data-driven custom discs but adds complexity across versions. I'm also considering cutscene-style camera work using spectator mode tied to a moving display entity with teleport interpolation, though this remains a limited workaround rather than true cinematic camera control.

Moving on, I'm cataloging more feature gaps: generic server-selector menus (not possible without Bungee), basic anti-cheat checks like fly/speed detection, backpacks and extra storage requiring plugin-side item serialization, graves and deathchests, clan/faction/party systems, kill-count leaderboards, and custom crop farming which is constrained to tweaking vanilla crop growth since new crop blocks aren't feasible. I'm now looking at the Dialog API introduced in 1.21.7+ for building UI dialogs.

I'm checking resource pack retexturing of vanilla items, noting that overriding vanilla assets is discouraged, and confirming that a server-selector/Bungee-style proxy setup is simply impossible since there's no real network proxy here — so I'm marking that one unavailable and trimming my list down to around 64 solid entries. Now I'm mapping feasibility tiers against vanilla clients — full, resource-pack-dependent, partial, or client-mod-only — and cross-referencing version-specific capability facts: texture overrides are limited pre-1.21.4, item states don't work on 1.21.1, dialogs need 1.21.8+, creature customization is locked to the 26.x branch, and critically, the designer/javac classpath only verified working on 1.21.11 and 26.2 — a constraint I need to flag clearly.

Beyond that, I'm cataloging a long list of version-gated API details: mannequin NPCs needing 1.21.11, PlayerInputEvent timing, GameRule.PVP behavior, the Attribute enum-vs-interface split, datapack format differences across 1.21.1 vs 1.21.4+, four worldgen schema variants, and the 1.21.2+ additions like equippable/consumable components, setItemModel, and setTooltipStyle — while display entities and TextDisplay remain stable across all versions. Since 26.x isn't buildable yet, I'm marking everything on that branch as unavailable pending Cyrus support. Now I want to actually verify several of these API claims with javap against each version's paper-api jar, so I'm setting up a workspace on node-2 to run that comparison.

On node-2, I'm assembling API-only classpaths per version — using the gradle-resolved classpath for 1.21.11, server libraries minus the versions jar for 1.21.4/1.21.8, and for 1.21.1 I need to pull paper-api plus its library set from the cyrus-v6-library gradle cache, checking whether that cache already has a stored classpath record I can reuse instead of reconstructing it from the module/pom files.

def V(**over):
    """Per-version notes for an archetype: {version: [ {lane, availability, reason, substitute, minVersion} ]}."""
    out = {}
    for v, items in over.items():
        key = v.replace("_", ".").replace("v", "")
        out[key] = [dict(lane=i[0], availability=i[1], reason=i[2], substitute=i[3] if len(i) > 3 else None, minVersion=i[4] if len(i) > 4 else None) for i in items]
    return out

content.content:
## Phase 2 Capability mapping
**Purpose:** turn research into the typed contract and decide what Cyrus can honestly offer.
**Templates:** [templates/CAPABILITY-WORKSHEET.md](templates/CAPABILITY-WORKSHEET.md), [templates/ADAPTER-CHECKLIST.md](templates/ADAPTER-CHECKLIST.md). **Brief:** B1.

1. Fill `lib/cyrus/games/<id>.ts` (GameSupport: versions, install, verification, dangerous APIs, breakage risks,
   outdated signals, categories, sources, unknowns).
2. Fill `lib/cyrus/adapters/<id>.ts` (GameAdapter: artifacts with honest availability, toolchain, knowledge ref,
   versions, assetDelivery per kind, install, testLane, routeRules with honest limit messages). Maturity stays `planned`.
3. Fill the AssetProfile (formats, channel map, colour spaces, normal convention, max resolution, UV + skeleton policy,
   packaging, delivery strategy, worker class, required game files, legal with `reviewed: false`, validators, preview
   shader, catalog fit hints, motion capability). `validateAssetProfile()` must return no issues.
4. **Derive the capability manifest** (`lib/cyrus/onboarding/manifest.ts`, `new-game.ts <id> --manifest`): for each
   studio / tool (Texture, Sound, Model, Motion, Config, Data Pack studios; designers; creatures; library fit; import;
   Mod Packs + conflicts; Test Flight; install onto Nxeon servers; Server Doctor) the state **usable** (adapter supports
   it + a game emitter exists + its delivery / route is available), **planned** (something is missing, with the reason)
   or **hidden** (the game cannot use it; never shown to customers). Plus route availability, worker classes
   (linux-cpu / windows-tools / gpu), required game files (none / user-supplied / platform-licensed) and the **legal
   class per asset type** from the ledger (`lib/cyrus/assets3d/ledger.ts`; game-derived = job-only, never in a library).
5. List **contract gaps**: anything the shared types cannot express (see the cross-game list in CASE-STUDIES.md).
   Raise them; do not work around them silently.

**Exit:** files typed and validated; worksheet agrees with the derived manifest; contract gaps listed; health test green.

## Phase 3 Tooling decisions
### Maturity ladder
The exit criteria are code (`lib/cyrus/onboarding/health.ts` LADDER_CRITERIA); the test checks this table matches.

| Rung | Exact exit criteria |
|---|---|
| planned | Nothing built. Adapter file + GameSupport stub + record exist; every unknown is listed. |
| template | Canned / template output exists and passes the game's validator. |
| beta | Real AI build path: compile >= 90% over >= 20 builds, the safety scan runs on every build, eval run >= 20 measured prompts at >= 80%; owner gate G6-beta signed. |
| stable | Beta plus headless boot + functional flights >= 95% over >= 10 flights, one real-client day, legal reviewed by the owner (G7-legal) and a no-manual delivery path. |

The adapter's `maturity` may never exceed the record's `declaredMaturity`, which may never exceed what the evidence
proves. **Exit:** evidence recorded; maturity bump proposed. **Gate G6-beta** (for beta).

## Phase 7 Legal + security review
## Frugality rules
- One Sonnet pass per research area at about 10 pages; bundle areas for small games (three passes, not nine).
- Opus only for phase 2 / 4 / 8 build work; one owner per file; at most two agents at once per game.
- Reuse the case studies and the cross-game contract gap list; extend them, do not rewrite them.
- No paid model calls (eval runs, image / 3D APIs) without the owner's budget in the brief.
- Templates are cheap to fill on purpose: tables over prose, labels over paragraphs.

## How this playbook stays current
1. **Lessons learned after every onboarding.** The phase 9 exit (and any abandonment, hold or rejection) appends 3-8
   entries to [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) (brief L1): what happened, what it cost, the rule it implies, the playbook change.
2. **Versioned changes.** A rule change edits this file, adds a [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) entry and bumps
   `PLAYBOOK_VERSION` in `lib/cyrus/onboarding/types.ts` (major = a phase or gate changes; minor = a new template,
   checklist item or criterion; patch = wording). Records carry the `playbookVersion` they were brought up to.
3. **Docs coverage hook.** `test/cyrus-onboarding.test.ts` fails when the version differs between code, this file and
   the changelog; when a template or brief this file links is missing; when the ladder table or gate list here drifts
   from the code; when LESSONS.md loses its shape; and when any game record claims more maturity than its evidence.
   (There is no repo-wide docs-coverage test on `feature/cyrus-r2` today; when r46's docs work adds one, this file
   should be registered in it.)
4. **Quarterly review** by the owner of the scorecard weights and threshold against the games actually onboarded.
# Onboarding lessons learned

Appended after every onboarding (phase 9 exit) and whenever an onboarding is put on hold, rejected or abandoned
(brief L1 in templates/agent-briefs/REVIEW.md). Format per entry, newest last:

```
### L<n> <short title> (<game>, <date>)
What happened. What it cost.
Rule: the rule it implies.
Playbook change: the section that changed (+ version), or "none".
```

The first entries are retro-fitted from the work that predates the playbook (research files in
`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/` and the game readiness checklists).

### L1 Delivery decides the product, not the editor (multi-game research, 2026-10-10)
Research H found most "3D support" requests fail on delivery: Valheim, Rust and Fallout cannot push assets to players,
so a texture studio for them would build things nobody can use.
Rule: delivery path is criterion 1 (weight 20) and a knockout for manual-install-only games.
Playbook change: phase 0 scorecard (1.0.0).

### L2 Template previews are not a build path (Terraria / Valheim / Zomboid, 2026-10-08)
Three games got verified GameSupport files, generators and validators, but every output is template code and the
build service only builds Minecraft; their readiness lists "real AI generation path" as must-have item 1.
Rule: maturity `template` is a real rung with its own exit criteria; beta needs the real AI build path with measured
compile and eval rates.
Playbook change: maturity ladder (1.0.0).

### L3 Official pages can be unreachable; label it (Hytale, 2026-10-10)
Hytale's support pages returned 403, so the server-provider terms rest on host wikis (V-s); the AI-asset terms are
Rule: read every licence on the source's own page; pin and quote; re-check sources before each ingest.
Playbook change: phase 5 (1.0.0).

### L5 Ids differ between Cyrus and Nxeon (Zomboid, 2026-10-11)
Cyrus calls it `zomboid`; the Nxeon game family is `projectzomboid` (lib/games.ts). Any join between Cyrus records and
Nxeon servers needs an explicit mapping.
Rule: phase 8 records the Nxeon family slug next to the Cyrus id.
Playbook change: phase 8 touchpoint table (1.0.0).

### L6 Adapter data lags the code (Minecraft, 2026-10-11)
The Minecraft adapter still declares texture / sound / model delivery and `testLane.boot` as "planned" while pack
hosting, the studios and Test Flight exist behind flags. Honest for customers (flags are off), but it means the derived
manifest shows Texture Studio as planned for the reference game.
Rule: flipping a delivery flag on is incomplete until the adapter's availability flips with it (launch checklist).
Playbook change: none yet (tracked in IMPROVEMENTS.md).

minor = a new template, checklist item or scoring criterion; patch = wording. The top entry must equal

906 /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/BA-reference-mods.md
# BA: private reference-mod corpus and analysis (2026-10-11)

PRIVATE. Every item is third-party, private-only, game-derived-class reference. Nothing is redistributed, served, committed or pasted into Cyrus output; only script-derived aggregate facts leave the staging dir. Data: `/tank/cyrus-library-staging/_reference-mods/` (README.md, catalog.jsonl, analysis/aggregate.json, per_item.jsonl, scripts). Source: official Modrinth API v2 only, UA `nxeon-cyrus-research/1.0 (https://cyrus.my)`, ~3 req/s, sha512 verified, 0 hash failures, 0 429s. No model calls; JDK absent, so a small Python class-file parser did the constant-pool scan.

## Corpus
| Type | Files | Disk | Matched 1.21.1 / .4 / .8 / .11 | Licence mix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plugin (paper/spigot/bukkit/purpur/folia) | 173 | 508 MB | 121 / 133 / 136 / 151 | MIT 50, GPL 54, ARR 34, LGPL 11, Apache 7 |
| datapack | 141 | 178 MB | 81 / 45 / 47 / 81 | MIT 46, ARR 41, CC-BY-NC* 13 |
| resourcepack | 43 | 107 MB | 31 / 25 / 28 / 33 | ARR 20, MIT 8, CC/other 15 |
| other-loader (not-buildable-by-cyrus) | 29 | 123 MB | 14 / 1 / 2 / 15 | ARR 6, MIT 6, LGPL 6 |

Total 386 files, 1.05 GB (cap 25 GB). Plugin category membership (a plugin may be in several): utility 110, game-mechanics 75, management 46, adventure 40, social 27, equipment 25, library 21, decoration/economy/technology/transportation 17, minigame/optimization/storage 16, cursed/food/magic/mobs/worldgen 15. Datapacks: adventure 65, game-mechanics 60, utility 49, worldgen 36, equipment 25, mobs 23, others 10-19 each. Resource packs: vanilla-like 24, tweaks 16, modded 14, utility 10, themed 9, others 5-6.

## What real plugins do (n=173, top by downloads, so large and legacy-friendly: median 512 classes, 1.1 MB)
- api-version: 1.13 (32%), 1.21 (24%), 1.16 (9%), 1.19 (6%), exact 1.21.x (13%). Class major: Java 8 (60%), 21 (56%), 17 (33%).
- Most-used API classes: Player, PluginManager, Bukkit, Listener, Server, World, CommandSender, Location, BukkitScheduler (75%), Material, Block, ItemStack, YamlConfiguration (62%), NamespacedKey (58%), ItemMeta, ChatColor (51%), Component (39%). Top events (plugins): PlayerJoin 114, PlayerQuit 98, PlayerInteract 70, InventoryClick 64, BlockBreak 62, BlockPlace 51, PlayerMove 50, InventoryClose 39, PlayerDeath 39, EntityDamageByEntity 39.
- Scheduling: sync runTask-family 60%, Bukkit async 43%, ExecutorService 36%, CompletableFuture 32%, extends BukkitRunnable 26%, legacy scheduleSync* 24%, Folia region schedulers 42%.
- Persistence: NIO files 64%, YAML 62%, Gson JSON 53%, JDBC 37% (Hikari 5%, SQLite/MySQL/H2 each under 2% as direct refs), PDC 34%, Java serialization 22%, none 12%.
- Config: config.yml in 47%; median 47 keys, 8 top-level, depth 3; 85% commented; top keys debug, language, enabled, database, messages, storage.
- Commands: 53% declare commands (median 1); 58% have aliases; 39% set a permission field; permission nodes start with the plugin name 90%; depth 3 most common; frequent suffixes `*`, others, reload, admin, use, bypass.
- Deps: any depend/softdepend 64%; softdepend PlaceholderAPI 62, Vault 38, WorldGuard 27, LuckPerms 23, ProtocolLib 17, ViaVersion 14, floodgate 14.
- Telemetry/network: bStats 58%, update checker (modrinth/spiget/github) 28%, http/socket classes 64%. Reflection 66%, NMS/CraftBukkit 23%, Brigadier/Lifecycle commands 24%, paper-plugin.yml 10%, `libraries:` 10%, shading other packages 51%, Kotlin 2%.

## Top gaps vs Cyrus (sheets, prompts.js, rules, minecraft.ts, designer; word-match, 146/300 popular API classes mentioned)
1. Events used by 10-20% of plugins and absent from Cyrus text: PlayerChangedWorld, PluginDisable, PlayerCommandPreprocess, InventoryOpen, WorldLoad/Unload, ChunkLoad/Unload, Block Piston Extend/Retract, PlayerSwapHandItems, CreatureSpawn (+SpawnReason), PlayerFish, EntityShootBow, ProjectileLaunch, FoodLevelChange, SignChange, PlayerLogin/AsyncPlayerPreLogin, AsyncTabComplete.
2. APIs unmentioned: OfflinePlayer (49% of plugins), BlockFace, BlockState/BlockStateMeta, Chunk, SkullMeta, PotionMeta, BookMeta, DyeColor, Biome, Villager/merchant, ExperienceOrb, FixedMetadataValue (metadata), ServicesManager, Bukkit BossBar (BarColor/Style/Flag; Cyrus teaches only Adventure), InventoryType/InventoryView, PermissionDefault, ConsoleCommandSender, Bukkit.getConsoleSender, NamespacedKey.fromString, Block.getRelative/setType/getBlockData, isPrimaryThread.
3. Pattern conflicts (real plugins do it; Cyrus forbids or never mentions): networking, reflection/Class.forName (62%), NMS, Brigadier, Folia schedulers, bStats, shading, Vault/PlaceholderAPI/WorldGuard softdepends (no lane for new plugins), JSON/SQL storage (Cyrus teaches YAML only), legacy ChatColor.translateAlternateColorCodes (still 31%).
4. Datapacks: dialog, predicate (23%), item_modifier (18%), damage_type, worldgen structure/template_pool/processor_list (23%) and `execute`-heavy functions (66k `execute` vs 17k `scoreboard` lines) sit outside the spec; Cobblemon-style species/spawn packs skew the sample.
5. Archetypes with ~0 keyword hits in Cyrus text and eval: minigame arena/lobby/queue, party/guild/clan, moderation/punishments, region claims/protection, backpack/storage, machines/automation, custom blocks/furniture, entity-limit/lag tools, voice/proxy messaging.
Resource packs: models 42%, item/block textures ~40%, optifine CIT 30%, gui 26%, lang 19%, core shaders 9%, fonts 9%, custom sounds 5%; median zip 0.3 MB; none use custom_model_data files (the 1.21.4+ item-model path is the norm).

## Recommendations
- API sheets: add an events catalog (the ~20 above, cancel/async semantics), a block/world sheet (BlockFace, BlockState, Chunk), head/potion/book metas, OfflinePlayer (warn: name lookup is blocking), Bukkit BossBar equivalence, metadata API.
- Failure rules (precheck): Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(String) on main thread, Player.spigot(), translateAlternateColorCodes, Class.forName, PlayerMove without hasChangedBlock, async Bukkit calls.
- Templates: Gson JSON per-UUID store (Gson is on the classpath), PDC item tags, listener skeletons for the top 10 events.
- Coverage matrix: add rows weighted by category counts above (minigame, social, management, storage, technology, decoration).
- Eval set: one prompt per new event and per missing archetype, plus 1.21.1 enum-era variants; keep refusal cases for network/reflection/NMS.

## Not fetched / caveats
- Skipped >60 MB: puffradio (131 MB), cobblemon-music-pack (342 MB), cobblemon mod (139 MB).
- Plugin/resourcepack sets are smaller than the nominal quota (173, 43) because per-category tops overlap the overall tops; the `features`/`resolutions` resource-pack headers were not treated as categories.
- Top-by-downloads is skewed to big multi-platform projects (Simple Voice Chat, WorldEdit); several client-only mods leaked into other-loader (server_side optional). No compile check (no source). Relocated shaded libs inside the plugin package count as own code.

I'm also considering whether parties should merge into clans or stay separate, plus adding minigame queues, sign editing, and command aliases.

Expanding the list further: custom command handling, login/whitelist security, fishing mechanics, bow/projectile events, hunger, multi-world management via WorldCreator, player head shops, and rule books using BookMeta—each becoming its own archetype.

I'm expanding the plan's archetype matrix with more categories: automation plugins using hoppers and inventory events, lag-management tools with entity caps, voice chat (flagged as infeasible since it needs a client mod plus UDP), and party systems with chat and teleport features.

I'm also sketching golden example plugins that exercise additional events like world change, chunk loading, piston mechanics, and hand-swapping, plus a demand field tracking category plugin counts so the matrix table can be sorted by popularity.

For the sheets, I'm planning an events catalog covering blocks, worlds, meta types, and OfflinePlayer pitfalls, with Gson-based per-UUID storage and PDC tag examples. I'm also thinking through failure rules — things like deprecated OfflinePlayer lookups, PlayerMove handlers missing block-change checks — and considering whether precheck.js needs a file-level "unless" pattern to catch these cases properly.

I'm also weighing a narrow regex for detecting unsafe async Bukkit calls inside runTaskAsynchronously lambdas, though it feels fragile, and questioning whether precheck rules might end up blocking legitimate code patterns that happen to match.

Better to target compiler deprecation warnings directly, since those are precise signals — getOfflinePlayer(String), ChatColor's translateAlternateColorCodes, and Player.spigot() are all flagged as deprecated, so I can write warning rules keyed on those exact messages with suggested fixes.

I'm also thinking about how to structure the eval set: one prompt per new event and per missing archetype, plus refusal cases that test whether the model offers a safe, downgraded alternative instead of a flat refusal, per the coordinator's rule to explain limitations rather than decline outright.

Separately, I'm identifying gaps in the datapack lane coverage — predicate, item_modifier, damage_type resources, worldgen structure/template_pool/processor_list, and execute-heavy functions — as candidates for where I need to extend my work.

Now I'm planning the golden corpus build order, starting with chat/command plugins before moving into datapack and eval work. I'll draft the plugins in batches to manage scope, listing out candidate plugin IDs like mc-utility, mc-chatformat, mc-chatfilter, mc-channels, mc-mail, and mc-announcer as part of the first batch.

Cyrus would generate a small Fabric mod (keybind -> custom payload -> Paper plugin messaging; Java 21 for 1.21.x, Java 25 for 26.x), build it in a sandbox, and deliver an **.mrpack** (`modrinth.index.json` with `formatVersion`, `files` + `overrides/` for own jars; V [MP]) bundling Fabric loader, Fabric API, the mod and the server resource pack. Players open it in Modrinth App or Prism (U); a CurseForge `manifest.json` variant is a second export (U). Servers cannot push mods; one-click means download-and-import. Effort L (2-3 weeks MVP per version band).

## 3. Prioritised build order (value / difficulty)
1. Armor lane (6), tools/food/weapons component pass (7): S, big visible value.
2. Sounds, music, jukebox songs (16), recipes/loot/trades/advancements gaps (19).
3. GUI/HUD glyph font lane (11, 13, 25): M, unlocks "custom GUI" and chat emoji.
4. Furniture/props (3) then display-based custom blocks (2): M.
5. Dialog forms (12) for C+ (1.21.6+).
6. State-carrier custom blocks (1): M, needs Paper flags and sound override tests.
7. Enable BetterModel creature lane on 1.21.4-1.21.11 if the real flight proves it (4).
8. Mounts/vehicles/seats (5), cutscenes (20): M.
9. Skies/fog/weather (21), particle/VFX presets (17): M.
10. Core shaders and post FX (14, 15): L, ship last, one band at a time.
11. Client-mod lane + .mrpack delivery: L, only after demand is proven.

## 4. Top 10 risks
1. Version drift: shader format changes at 1.21.2, 1.21.5, 1.21.6 and 26.x; RP/DP minor formats from 1.21.9 (V [PF][SH]).
2. Pack merges: one shader or font file wins (V [OX]).
3. Entity-count blowups on small nodes; budgets all U.
4. Anti-cheat false positives on custom blocks, seats, vehicles (U).
5. Bedrock parity: hand-made packs, unstable custom blocks (V [GI][GB]).
6. Licence contamination: Oraxen and CraftEngine are GPL; use BetterModel (MIT) or clean-room only.
7. 250 MiB pack cap (V [SP]); declined packs.
8. 26.x needs Java 25 (V [J26]); 26.x plugins unbuildable until then.
9. State-carrier collisions with player builds; Paper flags are global.
10. Hardcoded behaviour invites impossible requests: show limits before spend.

#!/bin/bash
# Resolve the runtime libraries a BetterModel paper jar downloads on its FIRST start, so a Test Flight (no internet) can
# seed them. Owner/agent tool for the build host (node-2) only: it starts ONE throwaway Paper server WITH internet in a
# scratch dir (offline-mode, loopback port, no players), waits for "Done", stops it, then writes
#   <out>/seeds/bettermodel-<ver>-paper-libraries/...  (what Paper's library loader put in <server>/libraries)
#   <out>/seeds/bettermodel-<ver>-libby/...            (what BetterModel's libby put in plugins/BetterModel/.libs)
#   <out>/bettermodel-<ver>.libraries.json             (path, bytes, sha1, sha256; sha1 checked against Maven Central)
# Only files that are NOT already in the pinned Paper server's own libraries are kept.
#   resolve-libraries.sh <bettermodel jar> <paper dir with paper.jar> <java home> <out dir> <bm version>
set -euo pipefail
JAR="${1:?bettermodel jar}"; PAPER="${2:?paper dir}"; JH="${3:?java home}"; OUT="${4:?out dir}"; VER="${5:?version}"
W="$(mktemp -d /tank/nxeon-build/tmp/bm-resolve-XXXXXX)"; trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
cp "$PAPER/paper.jar" "$W/paper.jar"
cp -r "$PAPER/libraries" "$W/libraries"; cp -r "$PAPER/versions" "$W/versions"; [ -d "$PAPER/cache" ] && cp -r "$PAPER/cache" "$W/cache"
find "$W/libraries" -type f | sed "s#^$W/libraries/##" | sort > "$W/.base-libs"
mkdir -p "$W/plugins"; cp "$JAR" "$W/plugins/"
echo "eula=true" > "$W/eula.txt"
PORT=$(( 47300 + RANDOM % 90 ))
printf 'online-mode=false\nserver-ip=127.0.0.1\nserver-port=%s\nlevel-type=minecraft\\:flat\ngenerate-structures=false\nspawn-protection=0\nmax-players=1\n' "$PORT" > "$W/server.properties"
cd "$W"
( timeout -s KILL 600 nice -n 10 "$JH/bin/java" -Xmx1024M -jar paper.jar --nogui < <(while [ ! -f "$W/.stop" ]; do sleep 1; done; echo stop) > "$W/console.log" 2>&1 ) &
PID=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 540); do grep -q 'Done (' "$W/console.log" 2>/dev/null && break; kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 1; done
grep -q 'Done (' "$W/console.log" || { tail -40 "$W/console.log"; echo "server did not reach Done" >&2; exit 1; }
sleep 3; touch "$W/.stop"; wait "$PID" || true
grep -E "BetterModel|ERROR|Exception" "$W/console.log" | head -30 >&2 || true
mkdir -p "$OUT/seeds/bettermodel-$VER-paper-libraries" "$OUT/seeds/bettermodel-$VER-libby"
find "$W/libraries" -type f | sed "s#^$W/libraries/##" | sort > "$W/.all-libs"
comm -13 "$W/.base-libs" "$W/.all-libs" > "$W/.new-libs"
while read -r rel; do mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT/seeds/bettermodel-$VER-paper-libraries/$rel")"; cp "$W/libraries/$rel" "$OUT/seeds/bettermodel-$VER-paper-libraries/$rel"; done < "$W/.new-libs"
if [ -d "$W/plugins/BetterModel/.libs" ]; then cp -r "$W/plugins/BetterModel/.libs/." "$OUT/seeds/bettermodel-$VER-libby/"; fi
python3 - "$OUT" "$VER" <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, os, sys, urllib.request
out, ver = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
def files(seed):
    base = os.path.join(out, "seeds", seed); res = []
    for d, _, fs in os.walk(base):
        for f in sorted(fs):
            p = os.path.join(d, f); rel = os.path.relpath(p, base); b = open(p, "rb").read()
            sha1 = hashlib.sha1(b).hexdigest(); src = "https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/" + rel; ok = None
            try: ok = urllib.request.urlopen(src + ".sha1", timeout=20).read().decode().split()[0].strip() == sha1
            except Exception: ok = None
            res.append({"path": rel, "bytes": len(b), "sha1": sha1, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest(), "source": src if ok else None, "mavenCentralSha1": ok})
    return sorted(res, key=lambda x: x["path"])
doc = {"schema": 1, "plugin": "bettermodel", "version": ver, "notes": ["Resolved by services/modbuilder/tools/bettermodel/resolve-libraries.sh: first start of the pinned jar on a throwaway Paper server on node-2 with internet; files not already in the Paper server's own libraries. mavenCentralSha1 = the published .sha1 on repo1.maven.org matched (null = not on Maven Central, e.g. libby relocated jars or another repository)."],
       "paperLibraries": {"target": "libraries", "seed": f"bettermodel-{ver}-paper-libraries", "files": files(f"bettermodel-{ver}-paper-libraries")},
       "libby": {"target": "plugins/BetterModel/.libs", "seed": f"bettermodel-{ver}-libby", "files": files(f"bettermodel-{ver}-libby")}}
open(os.path.join(out, f"bettermodel-{ver}.libraries.json"), "w").write(json.dumps(doc, indent=1) + "\n")
print(json.dumps({"paperLibraries": len(doc["paperLibraries"]["files"]), "libby": len(doc["libby"]["files"]), "notOnCentral": sum(1 for g in ("paperLibraries", "libby") for f in doc[g]["files"] if not f["mavenCentralSha1"])}))
PY
