Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.thinking:
The build will take a while longer with all the plugin versions to compile and scan, so I'll use this waiting time productively to draft the new knowledge content from the BA recommendations, planning out the sections to add across the four sheets.

I'm thinking through coverage: events catalog, block/world APIs, item meta patterns, offline player lookups, data storage approaches (YAML vs Gson JSON), plugin integration via ServicesManager, and version-specific notes for 1.21.x features like PlayerInputEvent and Dialog.

Since gen-sheets.py treats markdown files as the source of truth, I'll edit the markdown directly to add a shared section plus version-specific lines rather than modifying the generator script. For failure rules, I'm checking whether things like Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(String) and Player.spigot() are actually flagged as deprecated by verifying against a negative compile corpus.

I also need ChatColor deprecation handled similarly for translateAlternateColorCodes, with the fix pointing to LegacyComponentSerializer.legacyAmpersand(). For playermove-no-changed-block, I realize I need to add an "unless" field to the precheck system so a rule only fires when a file-level pattern is absent -- specifically matching the PlayerMoveEvent handler signature unless it already checks hasChangedBlock, hasChangedPosition, hasChangedOrientation, or hasExplicitlyChangedBlock.

For async-bukkit-call, I'm writing a single-line pattern matching runTaskAsynchronously blocks that call unsafe Bukkit API methods like teleport, setType, spawn, getBlockAt, setBlockData, addItem, setHealth, sendBlockChange, or getNearbyEntities, accepting that multi-line async blocks won't be caught. For reflection, since Class.forName and similar calls are already blocked by the scanner, I want to add a rule that surfaces a clearer message pointing developers to the ServicesManager as the safe alternative for inter-plugin communication.

I'm also adding rules for version checks (point to Bukkit.getMinecraftVersion()), a merchant-menu-type warning for 1.21.4+, an nms-import rule blocking direct imports of net.minecraft or org.bukkit.craftbukkit internals in favor of the Paper API, and a networking rule blocking java.net/HttpClient usage with a note about the capability manifest.

For autofix rewrites, I'm considering mechanical fixes like the GENERIC_ prefix handling, but I'm wary of changes like Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(name) since it introduces nullable semantics, and ChatColor.translateAlternateColorCodes conversions to the newer component serializer since that changes the return type from String.

I want to check EntityType.fromName deprecation and Material.CHAIN handling, plus look for safe mechanical rewrites already present in autofix.js, like old Particle name mappings, before adding anything new.

content.thinking:
I'm considering mechanical autofixes for renamed Particle constants, like VILLAGER_HAPPY to HAPPY_VILLAGER or SMOKE_NORMAL to SMOKE, but noting that DUST would need accompanying DustOptions, making it riskier to apply automatically.

I'm extending this to similar enum renames in PotionEffectType and Enchantment, excluding ones that require extra data like SPELL_MOB or ITEM_CRACK. I'm also checking Material renames like CHAIN to IRON_CHAIN and EntityType.DROPPED_ITEM to ITEM as exact matches, while skipping ambiguous cases like GRASS or BOAT where multiple reasonable targets exist, and deciding to build a keyed rename table applied during the autofix step.

Rather than relying only on hand-written golden examples, I want to validate autofix coverage against a negative corpus of deliberate anti-patterns -- small source files reproducing common model mistakes like old particle names -- compiling them across versions and confirming precheck, warnings, and autofix each catch the resulting javac errors.

Going through the ordering, precheck runs before autofix, so particle-name autofix never fires since precheck already intercepts that case first -- meaning it's only useful when the rule is disabled. I'm cataloguing other anti-patterns to map against precheck/warning rules: deprecated offline-player lookups, chat color translation, legacy spigot messaging, unchanged-block move events, async Bukkit calls, merchant and chat event deprecations -- each needing its own rule or confirming an existing one covers it.

I'm checking whether scheduleSyncRepeatingTask is actually deprecated versus scheduleSyncDelayedTask, since I'm unsure the warning should trigger there. Then I'm mapping registry lookup methods like EntityType.fromName, Enchantment.getByName, and Sound.valueOf to warning rules fixing them via the newer Registry API, and considering extending the switch-pattern precheck rule to cover Villager.Profession and Biome enums on newer versions since those only have hard-coded knowledge entries rather than regex patterns.

For deprecated inventory/display APIs like createInventory and setDisplayName, I'm weighing whether to fail builds on these warnings at all — they still compile and run fine in 1.21.x, and failing them just adds repair cost without real benefit, so I want to limit hard failures to deprecations that are genuinely removed or cause real runtime issues, like blocking getOfflinePlayer calls or async chat event threading problems.

So I'm settling on warning rules specifically for getOfflinePlayer's blocking behavior, merchant API changes in 1.21.4+, and registry lookup methods deprecated for removal — leaving the rest as softer sheet guidance. Next I want to build out the negative test corpus with one plugin per anti-pattern, each paired with an expect.json specifying which layer (precheck, compile, warning, or scan) should catch it, and extend the harness with an antipatterns mode that reports which check layer flags each case.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Bundle mc-coverage: (re)writes the marked "coverage" block at the end of every sheets/<ver>.md. Idempotent.
# Every claim was compiled or javap-checked against that version's paper-api jar on node-2 (2026-10-11) by the golden
# corpus (services/modbuilder/golden) and its anti-patterns; inputs: the BA reference-mod report (most-used events/APIs
# absent from the sheets). Keep it short: the sheet is part of every build's system prompt.
#   python3 sheets/gen-coverage-sections.py services/modbuilder/sheets
import os, re, sys

VERS = ["1.21.1", "1.21.4", "1.21.8", "1.21.11"]
BEGIN, END = "<!-- mc-coverage:begin -->", "<!-- mc-coverage:end -->"


def ge(v, w):
    t = lambda s: tuple(int(x) for x in s.split("."))
    return t(v) >= t(w)


def block(v):
    L = []
    a = L.append
    a(BEGIN)
    a("## Events catalog (main thread unless ASYNC; cancel only what implements Cancellable)")
    a("- Players: PlayerJoinEvent, PlayerQuitEvent, PlayerChangedWorldEvent (getFrom()), PlayerTeleportEvent (getFrom/getTo/getCause), PlayerRespawnEvent, PlayerDeathEvent, PlayerInteractEvent (Action.PHYSICAL = pressure plates, fires repeatedly: debounce), PlayerInteractEntityEvent (check getHand() == EquipmentSlot.HAND), PlayerSwapHandItemsEvent (the F key; cancel it to keep the items where they are), PlayerToggleSneakEvent, PlayerItemConsumeEvent (cancelling also cancels eating: add extra effects one tick later), PlayerItemHeldEvent, PlayerDropItemEvent, EntityPickupItemEvent, PlayerFishEvent (getState() == State.CAUGHT_FISH, getCaught() is an Item), PlayerCommandPreprocessEvent (getMessage() starts with '/'), FoodLevelChangeEvent (getEntity() is a HumanEntity).")
    a("- ASYNC (never touch worlds/entities/inventories; hop back with runTask): AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent (before the player exists: event.disallow(AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent.Result.KICK_OTHER, Component)), AsyncChatEvent, AsyncTabCompleteEvent.")
    a("- Blocks: BlockBreakEvent (setDropItems(false)), BlockPlaceEvent, BlockDropItemEvent (getBlockState() = the broken block), SignChangeEvent (line(i) / line(i, Component)), BlockPistonExtendEvent / BlockPistonRetractEvent (getBlocks(), getDirection(): protect claims against pistons), BlockFromToEvent (flowing liquids), BlockBurnEvent, EntityChangeBlockEvent, InventoryMoveItemEvent (hoppers: fires constantly, keep it cheap).")
    a("- Entities: CreatureSpawnEvent (getSpawnReason(): NATURAL, SPAWNER, SPAWNER_EGG, BREEDING, COMMAND, CUSTOM = plugins; limit NATURAL/SPAWNER, never eggs or commands), SpawnerSpawnEvent, EntityTargetEvent, EntityShootBowEvent (getForce() 0..1, getProjectile()), ProjectileLaunchEvent, ProjectileHitEvent, PotionSplashEvent, EntityRegainHealthEvent.")
    a("- Inventory: InventoryOpenEvent (cancellable), InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, InventoryCloseEvent (save storage menus here), PrepareAnvilEvent.")
    a("- World / server: WorldLoadEvent, WorldUnloadEvent, ChunkLoadEvent (isNewChunk()) / ChunkUnloadEvent (never load other chunks inside them), ServerLoadEvent (after every plugin enabled), PluginEnableEvent / PluginDisableEvent (soft integrations).")
    a("")
    a("## Blocks, chunks, worlds, structures")
    a("- BlockFace: block.getRelative(BlockFace.DOWN), face.getOppositeFace(); yaw to a face: SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST for 0, 90, 180, 270. block.setType(mat, false) skips physics; getBlockData()/setBlockData(data, false); Material.STONE.createBlockData().")
    a("- BlockState: block.getState() is a SNAPSHOT (change it, then state.update()); block.getState(false) is a live view (no update(), do not keep it). Check `instanceof Container / Chest / Sign / CreatureSpawner / TileState`; a TileState has its own PersistentDataContainer (call update() after changing it on a snapshot).")
    a("- Signs: sign.getSide(Side.FRONT).line(0) (org.bukkit.block.sign.Side) or .line(0, Component).")
    a("- Chunks: block.getChunk().getChunkKey() (a long, unique per world), world.getChunkAtAsync(x, z).thenAccept(c -> ...), chunk.getEntities(), world.setChunkForceLoaded(x, z, true) (undo it).")
    a("- Worlds: new WorldCreator(\"name\").type(WorldType.FLAT).generateStructures(false).createWorld() (blocks the server for a moment); getServer().unloadWorld(world, true) after moving players out; never unload the first world.")
    a("- Structures (no schematic files): StructureManager sm = getServer().getStructureManager(); Structure s = sm.createStructure(); s.fill(corner, new BlockVector(x, y, z), false); sm.registerStructure(new NamespacedKey(plugin, \"hut\"), s); s.place(loc, true, StructureRotation.NONE, Mirror.NONE, 0, 1f, new Random()) (org.bukkit.block.structure).")
    a("")
    a("## Item metas, potions, books, trades")
    a("- Typed metas: item.editMeta(SkullMeta.class, m -> m.setOwningPlayer(offlinePlayer)); PotionMeta: setBasePotionType(PotionType.AWKWARD), addCustomEffect(effect, true), setColor(Color); LeatherArmorMeta.setColor(Color.fromRGB(0xD2501E)); BookMeta on WRITTEN_BOOK: title(Component), author(Component), pages(List<Component>). Open a book without an item: player.openBook(net.kyori.adventure.inventory.Book.book(title, author, pages)).")
    a("- Brewing recipes: Bukkit.getPotionBrewer().addPotionMix(new io.papermc.paper.potion.PotionMix(key, result, new RecipeChoice.ExactChoice(input), new RecipeChoice.MaterialChoice(Material.X))); removePotionMix(key) in onDisable.")
    a("- Villager trades: new MerchantRecipe(result, maxUses) + addIngredient(stack); villager.getRecipes() is a copy: build a list and setRecipes(list); VillagerAcquireTradeEvent when it gains a trade.")
    if ge(v, "1.21.4"):
        a("- Custom trade menu on this version: Merchant m = Bukkit.createMerchant(); m.setRecipes(list); MenuType.MERCHANT.builder().title(Component.text(\"Shop\")).merchant(m).checkReachable(false).build(player).open(); (org.bukkit.inventory.MenuType). Bukkit.createMerchant(Component) and player.openMerchant(merchant, true) are deprecated here.")
    else:
        a("- Custom trade menu on 1.21.1: Merchant m = Bukkit.createMerchant(Component.text(\"Shop\")); m.setRecipes(list); player.openMerchant(m, true). (There is no title-less createMerchant() or MenuType merchant builder on 1.21.1.)")
    if not ge(v, "1.21.4"):
        a("- 1.21.1 ItemMeta has no customName(Component): name items with displayName(Component).")
    a("")
    a("## Players by name, data, other plugins, displays")
    a("- NEVER Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(String name): it can block the server on a web lookup. Online: Bukkit.getPlayerExact(name). Known offline: Bukkit.getOfflinePlayerIfCached(name) (null if they never joined). Store players by UUID; Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(UUID) is safe (getName() may be null).")
    a("- Data: YamlConfiguration files for small data. Per-player data that grows: one JSON file per UUID with com.google.gson.Gson (on the classpath) at getDataFolder()/players/<uuid>.json; load on join, save on quit and on a timer; do the file IO in runTaskAsynchronously on a COPY of the data.")
    a(f"- Tags on items/entities/blocks: PersistentDataContainer only. setMetadata/FixedMetadataValue is in memory (gone after a restart){' and deprecated on 1.21.11' if ge(v, '1.21.11') else ''}.")
    a("- Offer an API to other plugins: getServer().getServicesManager().register(MyApi.class, impl, this, ServicePriority.Normal); others read it with getServicesManager().load(MyApi.class) (null if absent); unregisterAll(this) in onDisable. Optional plugin present: getServer().getPluginManager().getPlugin(\"Name\") != null. No reflection (the safety scan blocks it).")
    a("- Keyed Bukkit boss bar (stays in the world across reloads): Bukkit.createBossBar(new NamespacedKey(plugin, \"info\"), \"title\", BarColor.BLUE, BarStyle.SEGMENTED_10); remove with Bukkit.removeBossBar(key) in onDisable. Prefer the Adventure BossBar for per-player bars.")
    a("- Tab list: player.sendPlayerListHeaderAndFooter(header, footer); player.playerListName(Component).")
    a("- Display entities: world.spawn(loc, TextDisplay.class, d -> { d.text(c); d.setBillboard(Display.Billboard.CENTER); }) (holograms), ItemDisplay (props/furniture: setItemStack, setTransformation(new Transformation(new Vector3f(), new AxisAngle4f(rad, 0, 1, 0), new Vector3f(1, 1, 1), new AxisAngle4f())) with org.joml), Interaction (a click box: setInteractionWidth/Height, setResponsive(true), clicks arrive as PlayerInteractEntityEvent; a player can ride it as a seat). setTeleportDuration(ticks) makes teleports smooth (camera paths: player.setSpectatorTarget(display) in SPECTATOR mode, restore the game mode afterwards). Tag yours with PDC and remove them on clear.")
    a("- Player.isOnGround() is deprecated (the client reports it): check the block below or the velocity instead.")
    if ge(v, "1.21.4"):
        a("- Steering a ridden entity: player.getCurrentInput() (org.bukkit.Input: isForward, isBackward, isLeft, isRight, isJump, isSneak, isSprint) or PlayerInputEvent; armour changes: EntityEquipmentChangedEvent or com.destroystokyo.paper.event.player.PlayerArmorChangeEvent (re-check one tick later).")
    else:
        a("- 1.21.1 has no PlayerInputEvent / getCurrentInput (no steering of custom mounts: use vanilla rideables) and no EntityEquipmentChangedEvent: use com.destroystokyo.paper.event.player.PlayerArmorChangeEvent and re-check one tick later. Biome is an enum here.")
    if ge(v, "1.21.8"):
        a("- Dialog screens (forms, confirmations): io.papermc.paper.dialog.Dialog with player.showDialog(dialog) exist on this version.")
    else:
        a(f"- No Dialog API on {v}: use a chest menu for forms and confirmations.")
    if ge(v, "1.21.11"):
        a("- Player-shaped NPCs without packets: org.bukkit.entity.Mannequin (1.21.11). Gamerules: org.bukkit.GameRules.* (GameRule.* constants are deprecated for removal; DO_DAYLIGHT_CYCLE -> ADVANCE_TIME, DO_WEATHER_CYCLE -> ADVANCE_WEATHER, DO_MOB_SPAWNING -> SPAWN_MOBS, DO_INSOMNIA -> SPAWN_PHANTOMS, NATURAL_REGENERATION -> NATURAL_HEALTH_REGENERATION; KEEP_INVENTORY, MOB_GRIEFING, PVP keep their names).")
    else:
        a("- NPCs: a vanilla mob with setAI(false), setInvulnerable(true), setPersistent(true), setRemoveWhenFarAway(false), clicks via PlayerInteractEntityEvent (cancel the trade screen). Player-skinned NPCs need packets, which mods here cannot send.")
    a(END)
    return "\n".join(L)


def main(d):
    for v in VERS:
        p = os.path.join(d, f"{v}.md")
        s = open(p).read()
        s = re.sub(re.escape(BEGIN) + r".*?" + re.escape(END), "", s, flags=re.S).rstrip() + "\n"
        if v == "1.21.11":
            s = s.replace("- `world.setGameRule(GameRule.KEEP_INVENTORY, true)`; GameRule has KEEP_INVENTORY, DO_DAYLIGHT_CYCLE, DO_WEATHER_CYCLE, DO_MOB_SPAWNING, MOB_GRIEFING, FALL_DAMAGE, PVP (new in 1.21.11; SPAWN_CHUNK_RADIUS was removed).",
                          "- `world.setGameRule(GameRules.KEEP_INVENTORY, true)` with org.bukkit.GameRules (the GameRule.* constants are deprecated for removal in 1.21.11; see the gamerule names below). PVP is new in 1.21.11; SPAWN_CHUNK_RADIUS was removed.")
        open(p, "w").write(s + "\n" + block(v) + "\n")
        print(p, len(s.split()) + len(block(v).split()), "words")


main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

content.thinking:
I'm checking the build script substitutes the API version into plugin.yml correctly, and verifying whether the fixture compiled against BetterModel 2.2.0's API actually matches its real usage patterns like modelKeys, modelOrNull, and ModelRenderer.

While the compile runs, I'm shifting to lane-gap design, starting with the armor lane. The goal is an equippable component with proper asset IDs and worn layer textures, so I'm thinking through extending the texture DSL to support armor layers — specifically a parametric generator that builds armor sets from a color palette and pattern preset (plate, scale, robe, leather) drawn onto the standard vanilla 64x32 UV layout, since hand-authoring that UV layout per-pixel would be too hard but a deterministic generator from colors is tractable and valuable.

I'm also mapping out pack emission details — the equipment JSON structure and texture file paths for humanoid and humanoid_leggings layers — plus noting that the asset path layout shifted between 1.21.2/1.21.3 (models/equipment) and 1.21.4+ (assets/<ns>/equipment/). Since the buildable target versions are all 1.21.4 and later, they should share the same layout, but I want to verify this against the vanilla version index rather than assume.

I realize the server jar doesn't ship client resource assets, so equipment textures can't be confirmed from what's on disk — I'd need the private vanilla client index, which may only cover 26.1.2. On the plugin side, I'm thinking through how EquippableComponent's slot and model setters work in Paper 1.21.4, and how a test would read back the component server-side; since there's no client to render against, the honest conclusion is that pack correctness can be schema-validated but not visually verified.

For tools/food/weapon data components, I'm weighing whether to build this into the heavier item designer pipeline versus keeping it lighter as a documented knowledge section plus a golden "mc-components" example plugin that compiles and flight-tests across versions — the latter seems cheaper and more realistic to maintain.

For the datapack side, I'm thinking through enchantment effects (post_attack, attributes), predicates, item_modifiers, damage_type, and jukebox_song — these follow the existing emitter/validator pattern closely and deliver strong value for custom enchantments, discs, and death messages, at moderate effort.

For custom blocks, I'm considering the classic note-block carrier trick: blockstate JSON mapping note-block variants to custom models, paired with plugin logic that cancels physics and sets the right instrument/note on placement.

This requires a server config change (disabling noteblock updates in paper-global.yml, needing a restart) and demands overriding the entire vanilla note_block blockstate file — all ~800 variants — so the emitter has to emit the full file including vanilla models for unused states, or vanilla note blocks break visually. It's complex but valuable, whereas display-entity blocks are simpler and already partly exist via the motion lane and golden furniture work.

Other possible additions: a glyph-based menu background for the HUD/chest GUI designer (medium effort), and wiring BetterModel support for 1.21.x behind the CYRUS_CREATURES flag as a catalog entry. Given the token budget available, I'll sequence the work: finish the four-version flight testing and documentation for step 2 and commit, then tackle BetterModel 1.21.x wiring and flight testing as part of that same effort.

Then I'll move through datapack emitters for enchantment effects, damage types, and jukebox songs with predicates/item modifiers, followed by the armor lane with equipment texture generation and pack emission, then the item components sheet, and if time allows, note-block custom blocks and the glyph GUI feature. After that I'll circle back to step 4 evaluation and step 5 documentation. Let me check how the background tasks are progressing.

I'm wondering whether jspecify was excluded because it's already present in Paper's base server libraries, and whether the flight runner's server directory actually includes Paper's own libraries folder alongside the pinned paperclip setup.

Maybe the issue is that base libraries only contain jars, not poms, so the resolver's comm diff kept the new pom but dropped the jar since it already exists in base—but if the flight's libraries dir doesn't actually have that jar copied over, it'll show as absent. The simplest fix seems to be adjusting the resolver so that whenever a new file appears in a directory, all sibling files in that same directory get included too, rather than relying purely on the base/new diff.

# Nxeon-managed BetterModel 3.5.0 configuration (written by Nxeon; lib/cyrus/managed/bettermodel-config.yml).
# Changed from the plugin's defaults: metrics false, version-check false (no phoning home), module.player-animation
# false (Cyrus creatures do not use player models; the generated pack drops ~4,000 limb files), merge-with-external-
# resources false (Nxeon hosts BetterModel's pack as its own entry next to each mod's pack). Everything else is default.
# BetterModel Configuration
#
# This file contains all the configuration options for the BetterModel plugin.
# For detailed information on each option, please refer to the official documentation.

# Debugging options for development and troubleshooting.
# Enable these only if you are diagnosing issues.
debug:
  # Toggles debug messages for hitbox creation and interaction.
  hitbox: false
  # Toggles detailed stack traces for exceptions handled by the plugin.
  exception: false
  # Toggles debug messages related to resource pack generation.
  pack: false
  # Toggles debug messages for model tracker lifecycle and updates.
  tracker: false

# Visual indicator settings.
indicator:
  # Shows a progress bar during resource pack generation.
  progress_bar: true

# Core feature modules.
# Disable modules you don't need to save resources.
module:
  # Enables general entity models.
  model: true
  # Enables player-specific animations and models (e.g., custom limbs).
  player-animation: false

# Resource pack generation settings.
pack:
  # Obfuscates model and texture names in the resource pack to prevent easy extraction.
  use-obfuscation: true

# Toggles metrics collection via bStats (https://bstats.org/plugin/bukkit/BetterModel/24237).
# Disabling this helps us less to improve the plugin.
metrics: false

# Enables sight-trace culling: models are only rendered if there is a clear line of sight.
sight-trace: true

# Merges the generated resource pack with packs from other plugins.
merge-with-external-resources: false

# The base item used for custom model data.
# It's recommended to use an item that is not commonly used for other purposes.
item: leather_horse_armor

# Maximum distance (in blocks) for sending animation packets. -1 for default server view distance.
max-sight: -1
# Minimum distance (in blocks) before animation packets are sent.
min-sight: 5

# The namespace used for resource pack assets (e.g., assets/bettermodel/...).
namespace: bettermodel

# The format of the generated resource pack.
# 'zip': A standard .zip file.
# 'folder': A raw folder structure (useful for merging or debugging).
pack-type: zip

# The location where the resource pack file or folder will be generated, relative to the server root.
build-folder-location: BetterModel/build

# If enabled, models attached to invisible mobs will also be invisible.
follow-mob-invisibility: true

# If enabled, utilizes Purpur's AFK API to pause animations for AFK players.
use-purpur-afk: true

# Checks for new plugin versions on startup and notifies admins.
version-check: false

# The default movement controller for mountable models.
# 'walk': Standard ground-based movement.
# 'fly': Flying movement.
default-mount-controller: walk

# The time in ticks between inserted keyframes for smooth interpolation (lerp).
# Lower values result in smoother but potentially more resource-intensive animations.
lerp-frame-time: 3

# Prevents players from swapping hotbar slots if they have a custom player model or animation active.
cancel-player-model-inventory: false

# The delay in ticks before a player's original entity is hidden after a model is applied.
# This can help prevent visual glitches.
player-hide-delay: 3

# The number of packets to bundle together before sending.
# Higher values can reduce network overhead but may increase perceived latency. 0 to disable.
packet-bundling-size: 16

# Enables strict loading mode. If true, the plugin will fail to load models with unsupported features.
# If false, it will attempt to load them by ignoring unsupported parts, which may cause visual issues.
enable-strict-loading: false

content.thinking:
I'm double-checking my code placement is correct, then moving on to defining a techniques dictionary mapping each archetype to its relevant industry approaches, starting with custom block implementations using note block states and plugins like ItemsAdder or Oraxen.

For version caveats, I'm noting that custom blockstate models work even on 1.21.1 since block models don't require item model definitions, while display-based furniture needs item_model support in 1.21.4+ (or custom model data on 1.21.1). I'm also flagging gotchas: mining speed matching note block hardness, piston interactions, the global Paper config flag affecting all note blocks at once, and Bedrock compatibility requiring unstable Geyser custom-block mappings.

Now I'm mapping out custom mobs: using ModelEngine, BetterModel, or MythicMobs with an invisible vanilla base mob for AI and hitbox, with item_display bones driven by packets and animations from Blockbench. For Cyrus specifically, I'm thinking creature lane uses BetterModel 2.2.0 for 1.21.x (server-verified) or 3.5.0 for 26.x, with a fallback motion-core display-entity rig planned, while noting caveats around packet cost per bone per viewer, Bedrock clients seeing only the base mob, and hitbox size being tied to the base mob.

I'm also working through armor sets (equippable component with asset_id and layer textures for 1.21.4+, older versions needing dye/trims or model overrides), custom weapons/tools (item_model plus weapon/tool components and attribute modifiers), and custom food (consumable component for 1.21.2+, with food component behavior differing on 1.21.1).

I realize I need to correct an earlier claim: on 1.21.1, setting a FoodComponent via Paper's ItemMeta.setFood actually does make any item edible, since the food component alone handled eating pre-1.21.2 — my earlier statement that non-food items couldn't be made edible on 1.21.1 was wrong. Starting 1.21.2, eating behavior moved to the separate consumable data component, so setFood alone no longer makes an item edible; I need to verify this with a golden test comparing FoodComponent behavior across 1.21.1 and 1.21.4. I'm also noting custom enchantments now support post_attack and attribute effects, HUD glyphs rely on font glyph and negative-space tricks, and custom music uses sounds.json with jukebox song entries.

Now I'm cataloging more feasibility notes across features: cutscenes via spectator mode and display entity teleport duration, NPCs via vanilla mobs or the new Mannequin entity (1.21.9+) versus Citizens' packet-based fake players, holograms via text displays, worldgen via datapacks, custom crops using note blocks or tripwire as state carriers, and retexturing vanilla items using 1.21.4+'s component-based item model selection instead of OptiFine CIT. I'm also marking shaders as fragile and low-priority, confirming new block types with custom physics are impossible (only look-alikes), and noting particles, voice, and keybinds remain out of reach without a client mod — plus that Bedrock support via Geyser needs its own separate mappings. I'm about to compile all of this into a technical feasibility dictionary.

For roughly 25 asset-heavy archetypes I'm assigning specific techniques, while everything else defaults to "Paper API on the server — events, commands, PDC, scheduler — nothing on the client" with no caveat, and for the genuinely impossible features I'm tagging a "client mod lane" noting they'd require a future Fabric/NeoForge mod distributed via .mrpack.

While that process runs, I'll start on the next lane: building an armor generator. I'm looking into how the texture pipeline works—specs in assets/textures draw into PNGs, and pack.ts builds item models for the resource pack—so I can design a similar spec format for armor with a palette of base, shade, highlight, and trim colors.

I'm mapping out the vanilla humanoid armor texture layout (64x32 UV), working through the exact pixel regions for the head, hat overlay, body, and arms so the generator can paint correct shading and patterns onto each armor piece (helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots).

For painting, I'll fill each region with the base material, apply face-based shading (lighter front, darker back), layer on a pattern depending on type—horizontal bands for plates, offset checker for scales, dots for studs—then add a thin darker border and an accent stripe, while leaving the face opening clear on the helmet.

For the helmet, vanilla covers top/sides/back fully but leaves the front face mostly open, so I'll paint only a frame around that transparent zone. Boots only need the lower rows of the leg region painted since the model only shows that part, chestplate uses the body and arms of layer 1, and leggings use layer 2's legs plus the lower waist rows of the body.

Beyond the generator, I need to handle pack emission: an equipment JSON per item mapping humanoid and humanoid_leggings layers to the texture, plus the actual PNGs placed in the entity/equipment folders. I'm also considering auto-generating 16x16 item icons from the palette for helmet/chest/legs/boots instead of requiring manual textures, and on the plugin side wiring up EquippableComponent.setModel with the namespaced key and setItemModel for each piece, based on a leather or iron base item.

Now I'm tracking down where the pack builder actually lives -- it's in the texture pipeline (pack.ts and the service's textures module), and realizing a full end-to-end integration touches asset parsing, portal sync, and pack delivery, which is a lot. I'm settling on a minimal viable scope: build the armor generator and pack emitter with a validator and compiler function, write unit tests, do a real flight test of setEquippable on both plugin versions, and wire armor assets into the existing pack builder so they get included in builds -- leaving full service wiring as a stretch goal.

Given time constraints, I'm reconsidering priority order across features: custom blocks and furniture first, then mobs (already handled), then armor/tools/food/enchantments, then advanced GUI/HUD. For custom blocks, I'm working out the note-block state carrier approach -- vanilla's note_block blockstate uses a single model for all 800 state variants, so I'd need to override specific instrument/note/powered combinations with custom models while keeping sound behavior intact.

I need every unused state to still fall back to the vanilla model, which means generating full coverage across all 800 variant keys (16 instruments × 25 notes × 2 powered states) since partial variant matching leaves unmatched states broken, and multipart conditions won't cleanly express an "otherwise vanilla" fallback.

For the plugin side, I'm thinking through the Java logic: handling BlockPlaceEvent for custom block items via a PDC tag, setting the note block state's instrument and note values, cancelling NotePlayEvent, and preventing neighbor-triggered state changes using Paper's disable-noteblock-updates config or by cancelling block physics events.

I also need BlockBreakEvent to drop the custom item, and PlayerInteractEvent to cancel right-clicks on custom note blocks so they can't be re-tuned. The tricky part is vanilla note blocks — with Paper's flag enabled they keep their default instrument, but a player right-clicking to change the note value could accidentally push it into a reserved state space that overlaps with custom blocks, so I need a way to protect those reserved states without breaking normal vanilla note block tuning, which is what ItemsAdder seems to be navigating too.

Given these trade-offs, implementing this as a full designer component means writing Java code, verifying it compiles, and testing it in-flight, which is a multi-hour task. I'm also weighing display-entity based "props" as an alternative, placed via command rather than saved in the world like golden furniture.

I'll build the generator, validator, compiler check across versions, flight test, and unit tests, and honestly mark it as built but not yet wired into AI builds — that's roughly equivalent scope to a designer component. I'm planning similar treatment for worn armor equipment: generator, pack emitter, plugin snippet, and flight test.

I'm calculating that note blocks give 1150 possible states across 23 instruments (1350 on 26.2), and thinking through how a custom-block lane could allocate states based on which instruments are hard to reach through vanilla placement, since the instrument depends on the block below or a mob head above.

With Paper's disable-noteblock-updates flag, note blocks stop auto-updating instrument from neighbors, so I'm considering reserving the mob-head instrument states (zombie, skeleton, creeper, dragon, wither_skeleton, piglin, custom_head — 350 states total) since those only naturally occur when a head sits on top, and plugins like Oraxen handle this by forcing vanilla note blocks into a fixed harp/powered-false state while managing tuning themselves.

But the deeper issue is that note_block.json is a single-owner resource — if two mods each ship their own custom blockstate overrides, a naive pack loader that lets later packs win whole-file will hide one mod's blocks entirely, so a real solution needs a merge strategy across mods rather than simple overwrite. Given that complexity, I think the honest scope here is to build the generator for a single mod's state allocation rather than solving cross-mod merging right now.

For the actual implementation, I'm planning a TypeScript generator (~150 lines) plus a Java support class (~120 lines) compiled across four versions, with testing done via in-game commands to place blocks, verify state through execute/if checks, and query block info through a custom command rather than simulating full player break mechanics.

I'm sketching a spec schema for custom blocks—covering texture mappings, hardness tiers, drop behavior, and sound types, capped at 32 blocks per mod—and then thinking through how to allocate blockstates deterministically from each namespace's hash, weighing the collision risk against a more robust registry-based approach similar to how engine-core handles glyph block allocation.

Now I'm working out the allocation scheme using note block instruments and pitches to generate up to 50 state slots per mod, with the conflict engine flagging any overlaps between mods. Then I'm planning the emit step: generating blockstate JSON that routes reserved note block states to custom models while leaving the rest pointing at vanilla, plus the block and item model files needed to texture everything properly across different Minecraft versions.

For the Java side, I'm sketching a CustomBlocks template that handles placement (mapping a custom item via PDC to the right note_block state), breaking (dropping the custom item, cancelling vanilla drops, playing sounds), and protecting the block from note-play events, interactions, piston pushes, and explosions — plus a test command for giving/placing/inspecting these blocks.

I want golden tests across multiple Paper versions, verifying the generated plugin compiles and runs correctly. I'm also confirming the Bukkit API details: NoteBlockData's setInstrument/setNote/setPowered methods, the full Instrument enum (including newer entries like PIGLIN and CUSTOM_HEAD), and that Note takes an id from 0 to 24.

content.thinking:
1.21.11 passes everything, but 1.21.8 fails only on the damage check with "No entity was found" — maybe the zombie, summoned at y=101 in daylight, burns to death before the check runs, since older difficulty settings could let it ignite and die quickly.

I'm wondering if switching to a non-burning mob like a husk, or tagging a summoned entity and checking with a tag-based selector instead, would avoid this despawn/death issue entirely.

Actually, the timing doesn't fit a burn-death explanation since that takes several seconds, not 250ms. I'm now suspecting the "no entity found" result might be a tick-sync issue — maybe on 1.21.8 and earlier, a freshly summoned entity isn't queryable by `@e` until the next tick processes, and RCON commands sent in quick succession could be hitting that gap, even though 5 ticks should normally be enough. I also want to check whether the zombie at y=101 is actually landing somewhere unexpected on the flat world, since NoAI doesn't disable gravity, so it could be falling away from where I expect it to be.

To debug this cleanly, I'll swap the test entity to an armor stand with a tag so damage checks are simpler, and rerun across the three versions since the tests are fast anyway.

I'm puzzled why the summoned entity disappears on older versions but not the newer one — it could be a difficulty setting issue, since peaceful mode removes hostile mobs like husks, but I confirmed difficulty was set to easy. Maybe the real culprit is related to chunk loading at the origin coordinates.

Another angle: perhaps "spawn-monsters=false" in server.properties behaves differently pre-1.21.9, where it might actually cause existing hostile mobs to despawn each tick rather than just blocking natural spawning, whereas in 1.21.9+ this became a gamerule that only affects spawning, not despawning of already-summoned entities. That version split lines up exactly with the ≤1.21.8 versus 1.21.11 behavior I'm seeing.

Simplest practical fix is to sidestep the whole mystery by testing the damage logic on a non-hostile entity like a cow instead of a zombie, since the discard behavior seems tied specifically to hostile mob despawn checks rather than anything affecting general LivingEntities.

# usage: stagehunks.py <file> <comma-separated hunk start lines (old side) to stage>
import subprocess, sys, re
f, keep = sys.argv[1], set(sys.argv[2].split(","))
d = subprocess.check_output(["git", "diff", "-U0", "--", f]).decode()
head, *hunks = re.split(r"(?m)^(?=@@ )", d)
sel = [h for h in hunks if re.match(r"@@ -(\d+)", h).group(1) in keep]
patch = head + "".join(sel)
p = subprocess.run(["git", "apply", "--cached", "--unidiff-zero", "-"], input=patch.encode())
sys.exit(p.returncode)
EOF
echo ok

For commit 2, I'm sorting out which golden corpus and knowledge files belong together — the golden directories excluding the noteblocks/armor plugins (those go to step 3), the results/findings/antipattern files, the golden-flight script, the coverage sheets and generator, the failure rules and precheck/autofix scripts, specific hunks in server.js and prompts.js, the testflight library and its test files, and the minecraft-coverage matrix files including the doc and test updates. # AZ: Minecraft coverage bundle (2026-10-11)

Branch `feature/cyrus-mc-coverage` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-mc1`, from main 22cfdfd90e). Five commits. Not merged, not deployed, no flag flipped, no migration, no paid model call.

## What landed
1. **Coverage matrix**: 85 archetypes (BA reference-corpus demand weights, BB vanilla techniques) with lanes, technique, per-version support, caveats, Bedrock, Cyrus path, planner limits. `lib/cyrus/adapters/minecraft-coverage.json` is a `cyrus.capabilities.v1` catalogue (per-version `{lane, availability, reason, substitute, minVersion}`), rendered to `docs/cyrus/minecraft-coverage.md`. Playbook 1.1.0: a complete catalogue is required before a game leaves `planned` (LESSONS L7).
2. **Golden corpus**: 65 reference plugins + 13 anti-patterns (`services/modbuilder/golden`), run through the service's own checks and one Test Flight per version.
3. **Lane gaps, built and flown**: BetterModel 2.2.0 creatures on 1.21.x; data pack enchantment `postAttack`/`attributes`, `damage_type`, `jukebox_song`, `predicate`, `item_modifier`; note-block custom blocks; worn custom armor.
4. **Eval**: 103 coverage prompts (+6 safe-alternative, +8 bugfix), lane-selection accuracy, per-category scoring, `coverage-first` preset.

## Pass matrix (final, after fixes)
| | compile | scan | boot (Test Flight) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.21.1 | 64/64 | 64 (1 warn) | 64/64 |
| 1.21.4 | 65/65 | 65 (1 warn) | 65/65 |
| 1.21.8 | 65/65 | 65 (1 warn) | 65/65 |
| 1.21.11 | 65/65 | 65 (1 warn) | 65/65 |
The warning is the documented runtime permission grant (ranks). Mounts are 1.21.4+ only. Data pack lane: passed on all four. BetterModel 2.2.0: passed on all four. Anti-patterns: 13/13 caught by the expected layer.

## Findings fixed in the knowledge
1.21.11 deprecates every `GameRule.*` for removal (new `GameRules`, renames: sheet + warning rule + deterministic autofix); merchant API deprecated on 1.21.4+; food eat time moved to the consumable component (1.21.1 differs); `setFireResistant`, metadata API and `isOnGround` deprecated; `customName` missing on 1.21.1; name-only ban profiles throw; 1.21.11 has no spawn chunks (entities unload); `#enchantable/sword` removed in 1.21.11; Test Flight misread wrapped `plugins` output (runner fixed). Sheets gained an events catalog, blocks/worlds, metas, OfflinePlayer, Gson/PDC/ServicesManager, displays; 13 failure rules (precheck `unless`); rule 5 now names the safe alternative.

## Impossible without a client mod (honest labels kept)
New block/entity/fluid types and non-cube collision, keybinds beyond vanilla inputs, render pipelines beyond core shaders, new particle types, minimaps/free-form HUD, voice chat. Also out: proxy networks, Votifier/webhooks/update checkers (no networking), packet NPCs (no NMS). Each archetype names the closest vanilla build.

## Ran vs not run
Ran: every compile/scan on node-2 (JDK 21, real API classpaths), 4 golden flights, 4 data pack flights, 4 BetterModel flights, javap probes, vanilla data generator for new id kinds, tsc, Cyrus suite. Not run: any real client; any AI build of the new lanes; the eval (recommended first run: 40 builds on 1.21.11 at Saka, $3.90-$8.90, plus 2 on 1.21.1 $0.16-$0.36); core shaders, glyph-background menus, the client-mod lane.

## Next
Wire `assets/blocks` and `assets/armor` spec kinds into the service and delivery (with the Paper note-block flag); rebuild the build image for the BetterModel 2.x API jars; merge with `fix/cyrus-live-test-1` (its catalogue lanes match this JSON; creature lane now follows the registry on 1.21.x; rules lane recall 35% is the planner's job).
